units.leftText: Now after the death of His servant Moses, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant, saying,
units.rightText: Now it came to pass after the death of Moses the servant of Jehovah, that Jehovah spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ minister, saying,

units.leftText: “Moses My servant is dead. Now therefore arise, you and all these people, and cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel.

units.leftText: I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.
units.rightText: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, to you have I given it, as I spake unto Moses.

units.leftText: Your territory shall extend from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great River Euphrates— all the land of the Hittites— and west as far as the Great Sea.
units.rightText: From the wilderness, and this Lebanon, even unto the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your border.
leftNotes: 1:4 That is, the Mediterranean Sea

units.leftText: No one shall stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so will I be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you.
units.rightText: There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life: as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee; I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
leftNotes: 1:5 Cited in Hebrews 13:5|HEB 13:5*

units.leftText: Be strong and courageous, for you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.
units.rightText: Be strong and of good courage; for thou shalt cause this people to inherit the land which I sware unto their fathers to give them.

units.leftText: Above all, be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Moses commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.
units.rightText: Only be strong and very courageous, to observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest have good success whithersoever thou goest.

units.leftText: This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. For then you will prosper and succeed in all you do.
units.rightText: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth, but thou shalt meditate thereon day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

units.leftText: Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.” Joshua Takes Charge
units.rightText: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of good courage; be not affrighted, neither be thou dismayed: for Jehovah thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

units.leftText: Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people:
units.rightText: Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying,

units.leftText: “Go through the camp and tell the people, ‘Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.’”
units.rightText: Pass through the midst of the camp, and command the people, saying, Prepare you victuals; for within three days ye are to pass over this Jordan, to go in to possess the land, which Jehovah your God giveth you to possess it.

units.leftText: But to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said,
units.rightText: And to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, spake Joshua, saying,

units.leftText: “Remember what Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you when he said, ‘The LORD your God will give you rest, and He will give you this land.’
units.rightText: Remember the word which Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded you, saying, Jehovah your God giveth you rest, and will give you this land.

units.leftText: Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan. But all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them,
units.rightText: Your wives, your little ones, and your cattle, shall abide in the land which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but ye shall pass over before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valor, and shall help them;

units.leftText: until the LORD gives them rest as He has done for you, and your brothers also possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your inheritance and take possession of that which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you on the east side of the Jordan.”
units.rightText: until Jehovah have given your brethren rest, as he hath given you, and they also have possessed the land which Jehovah your God giveth them: then ye shall return unto the land of your possession, and possess it, which Moses the servant of Jehovah gave you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrising.

units.leftText: So they answered Joshua, “Everything you have commanded us we will do, and everywhere you send us we will go.
units.rightText: And they answered Joshua, saying, All that thou hast commanded us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us we will go.

units.leftText: Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you. And may the LORD your God be with you, as He was with Moses.
units.rightText: According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only Jehovah thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.

units.leftText: Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him, will be put to death. Above all, be strong and courageous!”
units.rightText: Whosoever he be that shall rebel against thy commandment, and shall not hearken unto thy words in all that thou commandest him, he shall be put to death: only be strong and of good courage.

units.leftText: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim, saying, “Go, inspect the land, especially Jericho.” So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men as spies secretly, saying, Go, view the land, and Jericho. And they went and came into the house of a harlot whose name was Rahab, and lay there.
leftNotes: 2:1 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: And it was reported to the king of Jericho: “Behold, some men of Israel have come here tonight to spy out the land.”
units.rightText: And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to-night of the children of Israel to search out the land.

units.leftText: So the king of Jericho sent to Rahab and said, “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they have come to spy out the whole land.”
units.rightText: And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, that are entered into thy house; for they are come to search out all the land.

units.leftText: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. So she said, “Yes, the men did come to me, but I did not know where they had come from.
units.rightText: And the woman took the two men, and hid them; and she said, Yea, the men came unto me, but I knew not whence they were:

units.leftText: At dusk, when the gate was about to close, the men went out, and I do not know which way they went. Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!”
units.rightText: and it came to pass about the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out; whither the men went I know not: pursue after them quickly; for ye will overtake them.

units.leftText: (But Rahab had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out there.)
units.rightText: But she had brought them up to the roof, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.

units.leftText: So the king’s men set out in pursuit of the spies along the road to the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as they had gone out, the gate was shut. The Promise to Rahab
units.rightText: And the men pursued after them the way to the Jordan unto the fords: and as soon as they that pursued after them were gone out, they shut the gate.

units.leftText: Before the spies lay down for the night, Rahab went up on the roof
units.rightText: And before they were laid down, she came up unto them upon the roof;

units.leftText: and said to them, “I know that the LORD has given you this land and that the fear of you has fallen on us, so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.
units.rightText: and she said unto the men, I know that Jehovah hath given you the land, and that the fear of you is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.

units.leftText: For we have heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, whom you devoted to destruction.
units.rightText: For we have heard how Jehovah dried up the water of the Red Sea before you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were beyond the Jordan, unto Sihon and to Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.
leftNotes: 2:10 Or the Sea of Reeds
2:10 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: When we heard this, our hearts melted and everyone’s courage failed because of you, for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.
units.rightText: And as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more spirit in any man, because of you: for Jehovah your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.

units.leftText: Now therefore, please swear to me by the LORD that you will indeed show kindness to my family, because I showed kindness to you. Give me a sure sign
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by Jehovah, since I have dealt kindly with you, that ye also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true token;

units.leftText: that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and that you will deliver us from death.”
units.rightText: and that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and will deliver our lives from death.

units.leftText: “Our lives for your lives!” the men agreed. “If you do not report our mission, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the LORD gives us the land.”
units.rightText: And the men said unto her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business; and it shall be, when Jehovah giveth us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with thee.

units.leftText: Then Rahab let them down by a rope through the window, since the house where she lived was built into the wall of the city.
units.rightText: Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the side of the wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.

units.leftText: “Go to the hill country,” she said, “so that your pursuers will not find you. Hide yourselves there for three days until they have returned; then go on your way.”
units.rightText: And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers light upon you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.

units.leftText: The men said to her, “We will not be bound by this oath you made us swear
units.rightText: And the men said unto her, We will be guiltless of this thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.

units.leftText: unless, when we enter the land, you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and unless you have brought your father and mother and brothers and all your family into your house.
units.rightText: Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt gather unto thee into the house thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father’s household.

units.leftText: If anyone goes out the door of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be innocent. But if a hand is laid on anyone with you in the house, his blood will be on our heads.
units.rightText: And it shall be, that whosoever shall go out of the doors of thy house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head, and we shall be guiltless: and whosoever shall be with thee in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand be upon him.

units.leftText: And if you report our mission, we will be released from the oath you made us swear.”
units.rightText: But if thou utter this our business, then we shall be guiltless of thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.

units.leftText: “Let it be as you say,” she replied, and she sent them away. And when they had gone, she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
units.rightText: And she said, According unto your words, so be it. And she sent them away, and they departed: and she bound the scarlet line in the window.

units.leftText: So the spies went out into the hill country and stayed there three days, until their pursuers had returned without finding them, having searched all along the road.
units.rightText: And they went, and came unto the mountain, and abode there three days, until the pursuers were returned: and the pursuers sought them throughout all the way, but found them not.

units.leftText: Then the two men started back, came down from the hill country, and crossed the river. So they came to Joshua son of Nun and reported all that had happened to them.
units.rightText: Then the two men returned, and descended from the mountain, and passed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun; and they told him all that had befallen them.

units.leftText: “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands,” they said to Joshua. “Indeed, all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of us.”
units.rightText: And they said unto Joshua, Truly Jehovah hath delivered into our hands all the land; and moreover all the inhabitants of the land do melt away before us.

units.leftText: Early the next morning Joshua got up and left Shittim with all the Israelites. They went as far as the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over.
units.rightText: And Joshua rose up early in the morning; and they removed from Shittim, and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel; and they lodged there before they passed over.
leftNotes: 3:1 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: After three days the officers went through the camp
units.rightText: And it came to pass after three days, that the officers went through the midst of the camp;

units.leftText: and commanded the people: “When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God being carried by the Levitical priests, you are to set out from your positions and follow it.
units.rightText: and they commanded the people, saying, When ye see the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then ye shall remove from your place, and go after it.

units.leftText: But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between yourselves and the ark. Do not go near it, so that you can see the way to go, since you have never traveled this way before.”
units.rightText: Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go; for ye have not passed this way heretofore.
leftNotes: 3:4 2,000 cubits is approximately 3,000 feet or 914.4 meters.

units.leftText: Then Joshua told the people, “Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the people, Sanctify yourselves; for to-morrow Jehovah will do wonders among you.

units.leftText: And he said to the priests, “Take the ark of the covenant and go on ahead of the people.” So they carried the ark of the covenant and went ahead of them.
units.rightText: And Joshua spake unto the priests, saying, Take up the ark of the covenant, and pass over before the people. And they took up the ark of the covenant, and went before the people.

units.leftText: Now the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you just as I was with Moses.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that, as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee.

units.leftText: Command the priests carrying the ark of the covenant: ‘When you reach the edge of the waters, stand in the Jordan.’”
units.rightText: And thou shalt command the priests that bear the ark of the covenant, saying, When ye are come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan, ye shall stand still in the Jordan.

units.leftText: So Joshua told the Israelites, “Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the children of Israel, Come hither, and hear the words of Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: He continued, “This is how you will know that the living God is among you and that He will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
units.rightText: And Joshua said, Hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go ahead of you into the Jordan.
units.rightText: Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passeth over before you into the Jordan.

units.leftText: Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.
units.rightText: Now therefore take you twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man.

units.leftText: When the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD — the Lord of all the earth — touch down in the waters of the Jordan, its flowing waters will be cut off and will stand up in a heap.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of Jehovah, the Lord of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off, even the waters that come down from above; and they shall stand in one heap.

units.leftText: So when the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, the priests carried the ark of the covenant ahead of them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the people removed from their tents, to pass over the Jordan, the priests that bare the ark of the covenant being before the people;

units.leftText: Now the Jordan overflows its banks throughout the harvest season. But as soon as the priests carrying the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water’s edge,
units.rightText: and when they that bare the ark were come unto the Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brink of the water (for the Jordan overfloweth all its banks all the time of harvest),

units.leftText: the flowing water stood still. It backed up as far upstream as Adam, a city in the area of Zarethan, while the water flowing toward the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea ) was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.
units.rightText: that the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap, a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
leftNotes: 3:16 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over the dry ground, until the entire nation had crossed the Jordan.
units.rightText: And the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah stood firm on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan; and all Israel passed over on dry ground, until all the nation were passed clean over the Jordan.

units.leftText: When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all the nation were clean passed over the Jordan, that Jehovah spake unto Joshua, saying,

units.leftText: “Choose twelve men from among the people, one from each tribe,
units.rightText: Take you twelve men out of the people, out of every tribe a man,

units.leftText: and command them: ‘Take up for yourselves twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan where the priests were standing, carry them with you, and set them down in the place where you spend the night.’”
units.rightText: and command ye them, saying, Take you hence out of the midst of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, and carry them over with you, and lay them down in the lodging-place, where ye shall lodge this night.

units.leftText: So Joshua summoned the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe,
units.rightText: Then Joshua called the twelve men, whom he had prepared of the children of Israel, out of every tribe a man:

units.leftText: and said to them, “Cross over before the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to take a stone upon his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of Israel,
units.rightText: and Joshua said unto them, Pass over before the ark of Jehovah your God into the midst of the Jordan, and take you up every man of you a stone upon his shoulder, according unto the number of the tribes of the children of Israel;

units.leftText: to serve as a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask, ‘What do these stones mean to you?’
units.rightText: that this may be a sign among you, that, when your children ask in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones?

units.leftText: you are to tell them, ‘The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters were cut off.’ Therefore these stones will be a memorial to the Israelites forever.”
units.rightText: then ye shall say unto them, Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah; when it passed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off: and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever.

units.leftText: Thus the Israelites did as Joshua had commanded them. They took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe of Israel, just as the LORD had told Joshua; and they carried them to the camp, where they set them down.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did so as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the midst of the Jordan, as Jehovah spake unto Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel; and they carried them over with them unto the place where they lodged, and laid them down there.

units.leftText: Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the priests who carried the ark of the covenant stood. And the stones are there to this day.
units.rightText: And Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests that bare the ark of the covenant stood: and they are there unto this day.
leftNotes: 4:9 Some translators And Joshua set up the twelve stones that had been in the middle of the Jordan

units.leftText: Now the priests who carried the ark remained standing in the middle of the Jordan until the people had completed everything the LORD had commanded Joshua to tell them, just as Moses had directed Joshua. The people hurried across,
units.rightText: For the priests that bare the ark stood in the midst of the Jordan, until everything was finished that Jehovah commanded Joshua to speak unto the people, according to all that Moses commanded Joshua: and the people hasted and passed over.

units.leftText: and after everyone had finished crossing, the priests with the ark of the LORD crossed in the sight of the people.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all the people were clean passed over, that the ark of Jehovah passed over, and the priests, in the presence of the people.

units.leftText: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over before the Israelites, armed for battle as Moses had instructed them.
units.rightText: And the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses spake unto them:

units.leftText: About 40,000 troops armed for battle crossed over before the LORD into the plains of Jericho.
units.rightText: about forty thousand ready armed for war passed over before Jehovah unto battle, to the plains of Jericho.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they revered him all the days of his life, just as they had revered Moses.
units.rightText: On that day Jehovah magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they feared him, as they feared Moses, all the days of his life.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Joshua, saying,

units.leftText: “Command the priests who carry the ark of the Testimony to come up from the Jordan.”
units.rightText: Command the priests that bear the ark of the testimony, that they come up out of the Jordan.
leftNotes: 4:16 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: So Joshua commanded the priests, “Come up from the Jordan.”
units.rightText: Joshua therefore commanded the priests, saying, Come ye up out of the Jordan.

units.leftText: When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the Jordan and their feet touched the dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their course and overflowed all the banks as before. The Camp at Gilgal
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah were come up out of the midst of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet were lifted up unto the dry ground, that the waters of the Jordan returned unto their place, and went over all its banks, as aforetime.

units.leftText: On the tenth day of the first month the people went up from the Jordan and camped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.
units.rightText: And the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.

units.leftText: And there at Gilgal Joshua set up the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
units.rightText: And those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, did Joshua set up in Gilgal.

units.leftText: Then Joshua said to the Israelites, “In the future, when your children ask their fathers, ‘What is the meaning of these stones?’
units.rightText: And he spake unto the children of Israel, saying, When your children shall ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean these stones?

units.leftText: you are to tell them, ‘Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.’
units.rightText: then ye shall let your children know, saying, Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.

units.leftText: For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as He did to the Red Sea, which He dried up before us until we had crossed over.
units.rightText: For Jehovah your God dried up the waters of the Jordan from before you, until ye were passed over, as Jehovah your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before us, until we were passed over;
leftNotes: 4:23 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: He did this so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, and so that you may always fear the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of Jehovah, that it is mighty; that ye may fear Jehovah your God for ever.

units.leftText: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted and their spirits failed for fear of the Israelites.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Amorites, that were beyond the Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, that were by the sea, heard how that Jehovah had dried up the waters of the Jordan from before the children of Israel, until we were passed over, that their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 5:1 That is, along the Mediterranean coast; literally along the sea
5:1 Or until we had crossed over

units.leftText: At that time the LORD said to Joshua, “Make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again. ”
units.rightText: At that time Jehovah said unto Joshua, Make thee knives of flint, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.
leftNotes: 5:2 Literally again the second time

units.leftText: So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth.
units.rightText: And Joshua made him knives of flint, and circumcised the children of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.
leftNotes: 5:3 Gibeath-haaraloth means the hill of the foreskins.

units.leftText: Now this is why Joshua circumcised them: All those who came out of Egypt— all the men of war— had died on the journey in the wilderness after they had left Egypt.
units.rightText: And this is the cause why Joshua did circumcise: all the people that came forth out of Egypt, that were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness by the way, after they came forth out of Egypt.

units.leftText: Though all who had come out were circumcised, none of those born in the wilderness on the journey from Egypt had been circumcised.
units.rightText: For all the people that came out were circumcised; but all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way as they came forth out of Egypt, they had not circumcised.

units.leftText: For the Israelites had wandered in the wilderness forty years, until all the nation’s men of war who had come out of Egypt had died, since they did not obey the LORD. So the LORD vowed never to let them see the land He had sworn to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
units.rightText: For the children of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the nation, even the men of war that came forth out of Egypt, were consumed, because they hearkened not unto the voice of Jehovah: unto whom Jehovah sware that he would not let them see the land which Jehovah sware unto their fathers that he would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

units.leftText: And He raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones Joshua circumcised. Until this time they were still uncircumcised, since they had not been circumcised along the way.
units.rightText: And their children, whom he raised up in their stead, them did Joshua circumcise: for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them by the way.

units.leftText: And after all the nation had been circumcised, they stayed there in the camp until they were healed.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they had done circumcising all the nation, that they abode in their places in the camp, till they were whole.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you. Wherefore the name of that place was called Gilgal, unto this day.
leftNotes: 5:9 Gilgal sounds like the Hebrew for roll.

units.leftText: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while the Israelites were camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, they kept the Passover.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel encamped in Gilgal; and they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho.

units.leftText: The day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the produce of the land.
units.rightText: And they did eat of the produce of the land on the morrow after the passover, unleavened cakes and parched grain, in the selfsame day.

units.leftText: And the day after they had eaten from the produce of the land, the manna ceased. There was no more manna for the Israelites, so that year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan. The Commander of the LORD’s Army
units.rightText: And the manna ceased on the morrow, after they had eaten of the produce of the land; neither had the children of Israel manna any more; but they did eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

units.leftText: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in His hand. Joshua approached Him and asked, “Are You for us or for our enemies?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?

units.leftText: “Neither,” He replied. “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” Then Joshua fell facedown in reverence and asked Him, “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?”
units.rightText: And he said, Nay; but as prince of the host of Jehovah am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?
leftNotes: 5:14 Or and paid homage or and worshiped

units.leftText: The Commander of the LORD’s army replied, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
units.rightText: And the prince of Jehovah’s host said unto Joshua, Put off thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

units.leftText: Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
units.rightText: Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hand, along with its king and its mighty men of valor.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thy hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valor.

units.leftText: March around the city with all the men of war, circling the city one time. Do this for six days.
units.rightText: And ye shall compass the city, all the men of war, going about the city once. Thus shalt thou do six days.

units.leftText: Have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark. Then on the seventh day, march around the city seven times, while the priests blow the horns.
units.rightText: And seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

units.leftText: And when there is a long blast of the ram’s horn and you hear its sound, have all the people give a mighty shout. Then the wall of the city will collapse and all your people will charge straight into the city. ”
units.rightText: And it shall be, that, when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when ye hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him.
leftNotes: 6:5 Or fall under itself or fall flat; similarly in verse 20
6:5 Literally and the people will go up, every man straight ahead; similarly in verse 20

units.leftText: So Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and said, “Take up the ark of the covenant and have seven priests carry seven rams’ horns in front of the ark of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun called the priests, and said unto them, Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And he told the people, “Advance and march around the city, with the armed troops going ahead of the ark of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And they said unto the people, Pass on, and compass the city, and let the armed men pass on before the ark of Jehovah.

units.leftText: After Joshua had spoken to the people, seven priests carrying seven rams’ horns before the LORD advanced and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when Joshua had spoken unto the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before Jehovah passed on, and blew the trumpets: and the ark of the covenant of Jehovah followed them.

units.leftText: While the horns continued to sound, the armed troops marched ahead of the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard followed the ark.
units.rightText: And the armed men went before the priests that blew the trumpets, and the rearward went after the ark, the priests blowing the trumpets as they went.

units.leftText: But Joshua had commanded the people: “Do not give a battle cry or let your voice be heard; do not let one word come out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then you are to shout!”
units.rightText: And Joshua commanded the people, saying, Ye shall not shout, nor let your voice be heard, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout.

units.leftText: So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. And the people returned to the camp and spent the night there.
units.rightText: So he caused the ark of Jehovah to compass the city, going about it once: and they came into the camp, and lodged in the camp.

units.leftText: Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests took the ark of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the seven priests carrying seven rams’ horns kept marching ahead of the ark of the LORD and blowing the horns. The armed troops went in front of them and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns kept sounding.
units.rightText: And the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark of Jehovah went on continually, and blew the trumpets: and the armed men went before them; and the rearward came after the ark of Jehovah, the priests blowing the trumpets as they went.

units.leftText: So on the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
units.rightText: And the second day they compassed the city once, and returned into the camp: so they did six days.

units.leftText: Then on the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner. That was the only day they circled the city seven times.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that they rose early at the dawning of the day, and compassed the city after the same manner seven times: only on that day they compassed the city seven times.

units.leftText: After the seventh time around, the priests blew the horns, and Joshua commanded the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for Jehovah hath given you the city.

units.leftText: Now the city and everything in it must be devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies we sent.
units.rightText: And the city shall be devoted, even it and all that is therein, to Jehovah: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.
leftNotes: 6:17 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 18 and 21.

units.leftText: But keep away from the things devoted to destruction, lest you yourself be set apart for destruction. If you take any of these, you will set apart the camp of Israel for destruction and bring disaster upon it.
units.rightText: But as for you, only keep yourselves from the devoted thing, lest when ye have devoted it, ye take of the devoted thing; so would ye make the camp of Israel accursed, and trouble it.

units.leftText: For all the silver and gold and all the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into His treasury.”
units.rightText: But all the silver, and gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are holy unto Jehovah: they shall come into the treasury of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So when the rams’ horns sounded, the people shouted. When they heard the blast of the horn, the people gave a great shout, and the wall collapsed. Then all the people charged straight into the city and captured it.
units.rightText: So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.

units.leftText: With the edge of the sword they devoted to destruction everything in the city— man and woman, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.
units.rightText: And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, both young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the house of the prostitute and bring out the woman and all who are with her, just as you promised her.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the two men that had spied out the land, Go into the harlot’s house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her.

units.leftText: So the young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother and brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
units.rightText: And the young men the spies went in, and brought out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and all that she had; all her kindred also they brought out; and they set them without the camp of Israel.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites burned up the city and everything in it. However, they put the silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: And they burnt the city with fire, and all that was therein; only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, with her father’s household and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho. So she has lived among the Israelites to this day.
units.rightText: But Rahab the harlot, and her father’s household, and all that she had, did Joshua save alive; and she dwelt in the midst of Israel unto this day, because she hid the messengers, whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

units.leftText: At that time Joshua invoked this solemn oath: “Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho; at the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.”
units.rightText: And Joshua charged them with an oath at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before Jehovah, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: with the loss of his first-born shall he lay the foundation thereof, and with the loss of his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.

units.leftText: So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.
units.rightText: So Jehovah was with Joshua; and his fame was in all the land.

units.leftText: The Israelites, however, acted unfaithfully regarding the things devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was set apart. So the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
units.rightText: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted thing; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the devoted thing: and the anger of Jehovah was kindled against the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 7:1 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 11, 12, 13, and 15.
7:1 Achan means troubler; also called Acharin 1 Chronicles 2:7|1CH 2:7*.
7:1 Zabdi is a variant of Zimri; also in verses 17 and 18; see LXX and 1 Chronicles 2:6|1CH 2:6*.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-aven to the east of Bethel, and told them, “Go up and spy out the land.” So the men went up and spied out Ai.
units.rightText: And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, on the east side of Beth-el, and spake unto them, saying, Go up and spy out the land. And the men went up and spied out Ai.

units.leftText: On returning to Joshua, they reported, “There is no need to send all the people; two or three thousand men are enough to go up and attack Ai. Since the people of Ai are so few, you need not wear out all our people there.”
units.rightText: And they returned to Joshua, and said unto him, Let not all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai; make not all the people to toil thither; for they are but few.

units.leftText: So about three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai.
units.rightText: So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai.

units.leftText: And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, chasing them from the gate as far as the quarries and striking them down on the slopes. So the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
units.rightText: And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men; and they chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim, and smote them at the descent: and the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.
leftNotes: 7:5 Or as far as Shebarim

units.leftText: Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown before the ark of the LORD until evening, as did the elders of Israel; and they all sprinkled dust on their heads.
units.rightText: And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of Jehovah until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust upon their heads.

units.leftText: “O, Lord GOD,” Joshua said, “why did You ever bring this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be destroyed? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
units.rightText: And Joshua said, Alas, O Lord Jehovah, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over the Jordan, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to cause us to perish? would that we had been content and dwelt beyond the Jordan!

units.leftText: O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back and run from its enemies?
units.rightText: Oh, Lord, what shall I say, after that Israel hath turned their backs before their enemies!

units.leftText: When the Canaanites and all who live in the land hear about this, they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. Then what will You do for Your great name?”
units.rightText: For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and will compass us round, and cut off our name from the earth: and what wilt thou do for thy great name?

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Joshua, “Stand up! Why have you fallen on your face?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore art thou thus fallen upon thy face?

units.leftText: Israel has sinned; they have transgressed My covenant that I commanded them, and they have taken some of what was devoted to destruction. Indeed, they have stolen and lied, and they have put these things with their own possessions.
units.rightText: Israel hath sinned; yea, they have even transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: yea, they have even taken of the devoted thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also; and they have even put it among their own stuff.

units.leftText: This is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They will turn their backs and run from their enemies, because they themselves have been set apart for destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove from among you whatever is devoted to destruction.
units.rightText: Therefore the children of Israel cannot stand before their enemies; they turn their backs before their enemies, because they are become accursed: I will not be with you any more, except ye destroy the devoted thing from among you.

units.leftText: Get up and consecrate the people, saying, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Among you, O Israel, there are things devoted to destruction. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them.
units.rightText: Up, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow: for thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, There is a devoted thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the devoted thing from among you.

units.leftText: In the morning you must present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe that the LORD selects shall come forward clan by clan, and the clan that the LORD selects shall come forward family by family, and the family that the LORD selects shall come forward man by man.
units.rightText: In the morning therefore ye shall be brought near by your tribes: and it shall be, that the tribe which Jehovah taketh shall come near by families; and the family which Jehovah shall take shall come near by households; and the household which Jehovah shall take shall come near man by man.

units.leftText: The one who is caught with the things devoted to destruction must be burned, along with all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and committed an outrage in Israel.’” The Sin of Achan
units.rightText: And it shall be, that he that is taken with the devoted thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath; because he hath transgressed the covenant of Jehovah, and because he hath wrought folly in Israel.

units.leftText: So Joshua arose early the next morning and had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was selected.
units.rightText: So Joshua rose up early in the morning, and brought Israel near by their tribes; and the tribe of Judah was taken:

units.leftText: He had the clans of Judah come forward, and the clan of the Zerahites was selected. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward, and the family of Zabdi was selected.
units.rightText: and he brought near the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zerahites: and he brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man; and Zabdi was taken:

units.leftText: And he had the family of Zabdi come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was selected.
units.rightText: and he brought near his household man by man; and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

units.leftText: So Joshua said to Achan, “My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make a confession to Him. I urge you to tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto Achan, My son, give, I pray thee, glory to Jehovah, the God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.

units.leftText: “It is true,” Achan replied, “I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:
units.rightText: And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Of a truth I have sinned against Jehovah, the God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done:

units.leftText: When I saw among the spoils a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
units.rightText: when I saw among the spoil a goodly Babylonish mantle, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
leftNotes: 7:21 That is, Babylonia
7:21 200 shekels is approximately 5 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of silver.
7:21 50 shekels is approximately 1.26 pounds or 569.8 grams of gold.

units.leftText: So Joshua sent messengers who ran to the tent, and there it all was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
units.rightText: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent; and, behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it.

units.leftText: They took the things from inside the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.
units.rightText: And they took them from the midst of the tent, and brought them unto Joshua, and unto all the children of Israel; and they laid them down before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his oxen and donkeys and sheep, his tent, and everything else he owned, and brought them to the Valley of Achor.
units.rightText: And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the mantle, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them up unto the valley of Achor.

units.leftText: “Why have you brought this trouble upon us?” said Joshua. “Today the LORD will bring trouble upon you!” And all Israel stoned him to death. Then they stoned the others and burned their bodies.
units.rightText: And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? Jehovah shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire, and stoned them with stones.

units.leftText: And they heaped over Achan a large pile of rocks that remains to this day. So the LORD turned from His burning anger. Therefore that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.
units.rightText: And they raised over him a great heap of stones, unto this day; and Jehovah turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.
leftNotes: 7:26 Achor means trouble.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai. See, I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai; see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land;

units.leftText: And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set up an ambush behind the city.”
units.rightText: and thou shalt do to Ai and her king as thou didst unto Jericho and her king: only the spoil thereof, and the cattle thereof, shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves: set thee an ambush for the city behind it.

units.leftText: So Joshua and the whole army set out to attack Ai. Joshua chose 30,000 mighty men of valor and sent them out at night
units.rightText: So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai: and Joshua chose out thirty thousand men, the mighty men of valor, and sent them forth by night.

units.leftText: with these orders: “Pay attention. You are to lie in ambush behind the city, not too far from it. All of you must be ready.
units.rightText: And he commanded them, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in ambush against the city, behind the city; go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready:

units.leftText: Then I and all the troops with me will advance on the city. When they come out against us as they did the first time, we will flee from them.
units.rightText: and I, and all the people that are with me, will approach unto the city. And it shall come to pass, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them;

units.leftText: They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘The Israelites are running away from us as they did before.’ So as we flee from them,
units.rightText: and they will come out after us, till we have drawn them away from the city; for they will say, They flee before us, as at the first: so we will flee before them;

units.leftText: you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
units.rightText: and ye shall rise up from the ambush, and take possession of the city: for Jehovah your God will deliver it into your hand.

units.leftText: And when you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded! See, I have given you orders.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, when ye have seized upon the city, that ye shall set the city on fire; according to the word of Jehovah shall ye do: see, I have commanded you.

units.leftText: So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and lay in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
units.rightText: And Joshua sent them forth; and they went to the ambushment, and abode between Beth-el and Ai, on the west side of Ai: but Joshua lodged that night among the people.

units.leftText: Joshua got up early the next morning and mobilized his men, and he and the elders of Israel marched before them up to Ai.
units.rightText: And Joshua arose up early in the morning, and mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.

units.leftText: Then all the troops who were with him marched up and approached the city. They arrived in front of Ai and camped to the north of it, with the valley between them and the city.
units.rightText: And all the people, even the men of war that were with him, went up, and drew nigh, and came before the city, and encamped on the north side of Ai: now there was a valley between him and Ai.

units.leftText: Now Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set up an ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
units.rightText: And he took about five thousand men, and set them in ambush between Beth-el and Ai, on the west side of the city.

units.leftText: So the forces were stationed with the main camp to the north of the city and the rear guard to the west of the city. And that night Joshua went into the valley.
units.rightText: So they set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers-in-wait that were on the west of the city; and Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.

units.leftText: When the king of Ai saw the Israelites, he hurried out early in the morning with the men of the city to engage them in battle at an appointed place overlooking the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set up against him behind the city.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at the time appointed, before the Arabah; but he knew not that there was an ambush against him behind the city.

units.leftText: Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten back before them, and they fled toward the wilderness.
units.rightText: And Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness.

units.leftText: Then all the men of Ai were summoned to pursue them, and they followed Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
units.rightText: And all the people that were in the city were called together to pursue after them: and they pursued after Joshua, and were drawn away from the city.

units.leftText: Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel, leaving the city wide open while they pursued Israel.
units.rightText: And there was not a man left in Ai or Beth-el, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Hold out your battle lance toward Ai, for into your hand I will deliver the city.” So Joshua held out his battle lance toward Ai,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Stretch out the javelin that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thy hand. And Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
leftNotes: 8:18 Or javelin; twice in this verse, and also in verse 26

units.leftText: and as soon as he did so, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position. They rushed forward, entered the city, captured it, and immediately set it on fire.
units.rightText: And the ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand, and entered into the city, and took it; and they hasted and set the city on fire.

units.leftText: When the men of Ai turned and looked back, the smoke of the city was rising into the sky. They could not escape in any direction, and the troops who had fled to the wilderness now turned against their pursuers.
units.rightText: And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and, behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way: and the people that fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers.

units.leftText: When Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that smoke was rising from it, they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.
units.rightText: And when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, then they turned again, and slew the men of Ai.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, those in the ambush came out of the city against them, and the men of Ai were trapped between the Israelite forces on both sides. So Israel struck them down until no survivor or fugitive remained.
units.rightText: And the others came forth out of the city against them; so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side: and they smote them, so that they let none of them remain or escape.

units.leftText: But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
units.rightText: And the king of Ai they took alive, and brought him to Joshua.

units.leftText: When Israel had finished killing all the men of Ai who had pursued them into the field and wilderness, and when every last one of them had fallen by the sword, all the Israelites returned to Ai and put it to the sword as well.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness wherein they pursued them, and they were all fallen by the edge of the sword, until they were consumed, that all Israel returned unto Ai, and smote it with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: A total of twelve thousand men and women fell that day— all the people of Ai.
units.rightText: And all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai.

units.leftText: Joshua did not draw back the hand that held his battle lance until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
units.rightText: For Joshua drew not back his hand, wherewith he stretched out the javelin, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.
leftNotes: 8:26 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: Israel took for themselves only the cattle and plunder of that city, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
units.rightText: Only the cattle and the spoil of that city Israel took for prey unto themselves, according unto the word of Jehovah which he commanded Joshua.

units.leftText: So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolation to this day.
units.rightText: So Joshua burnt Ai, and made it a heap for ever, even a desolation, unto this day.
leftNotes: 8:28 Ai means ruin.

units.leftText: He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening, and at sunset Joshua commanded that they take down the body from the tree and throw it down at the entrance of the city gate. And over it they raised a large pile of rocks, which remains to this day. Joshua Renews the Covenant (Deuteronomy 27:1–10|DEU 27:1-10*)
units.rightText: And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until the eventide: and at the going down of the sun Joshua commanded, and they took his body down from the tree, and cast it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised thereon a great heap of stones, unto this day.
leftNotes: 8:29 Or He impaled the king of Ai on a pole

units.leftText: At that time Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,
units.rightText: Then Joshua built an altar unto Jehovah, the God of Israel, in mount Ebal,

units.leftText: just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: “an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used.” And on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings.
units.rightText: as Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, an altar of unhewn stones, upon which no man had lifted up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt-offerings unto Jehovah, and sacrificed peace-offerings.
leftNotes: 8:31 Exodus 20:25|EXO 20:25*; Deuteronomy 27:5

units.leftText: And there in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written.
units.rightText: And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote, in the presence of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.
units.rightText: And all Israel, and their elders and officers, and their judges, stood on this side of the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, as well the sojourner as the home-born; half of them in front of mount Gerizim, and half of them in front of mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of Jehovah had commanded at the first, that they should bless the people of Israel.

units.leftText: Afterward, Joshua read aloud all the words of the law— the blessings and the curses— according to all that is written in the Book of the Law.
units.rightText: And afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.

units.leftText: There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua failed to read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them.
units.rightText: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the assembly of Israel, and the women, and the little ones, and the sojourners that were among them.

units.leftText: Now when news of this reached all the kings west of the Jordan — those in the hill country, the foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon (the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites)—
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all the kings that were beyond the Jordan, in the hill-country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the great sea in front of Lebanon, the Hittite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard thereof;
leftNotes: 9:1 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea
9:1 That is, the Mediterranean Sea

units.leftText: they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
units.rightText: that they gathered themselves together, to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord.

units.leftText: But the people of Gibeon, having heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
units.rightText: But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done unto Jericho and to Ai,

units.leftText: acted deceptively and set out as envoys, carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.
units.rightText: they also did work wilily, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks upon their asses, and wine-skins, old and rent and bound up,
leftNotes: 9:4 Or set out with provisions

units.leftText: They put worn, patched sandals on their feet and threadbare clothing on their bodies, and their whole supply of bread was dry and moldy.
units.rightText: and old and patched shoes upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and was become mouldy.

units.leftText: They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”
units.rightText: And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We are come from a far country: now therefore make ye a covenant with us.
leftNotes: 9:6 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant; also in verses 7, 11, 15, and 16.

units.leftText: But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?”
units.rightText: And the men of Israel said unto the Hivites, Peradventure ye dwell among us; and how shall we make a covenant with you?

units.leftText: “We are your servants,” they said to Joshua. Then Joshua asked them, “Who are you and where have you come from?”
units.rightText: And they said unto Joshua, We are thy servants. And Joshua said unto them, Who are ye? and from whence come ye?

units.leftText: “Your servants have come from a very distant land,” they replied, “because of the fame of the LORD your God. For we have heard the reports about Him: all that He did in Egypt,
units.rightText: And they said unto him, From a very far country thy servants are come because of the name of Jehovah thy God: for we have heard the fame of him, and all that he did in Egypt,

units.leftText: and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan— Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth.
units.rightText: and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites, that were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon, and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

units.leftText: So the elders and inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions for your journey; go to meet them and say to them: We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.’
units.rightText: And our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spake to us, saying, Take provision in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them, and say unto them, We are your servants: and now make ye a covenant with us.

units.leftText: This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But look, it is now dry and moldy.
units.rightText: This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and is become mouldy:

units.leftText: These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they are cracked. And these clothes and sandals are worn out from our very long journey.”
units.rightText: and these wine-skins, which we filled, were new; and, behold, they are rent: and these our garments and our shoes are become old by reason of the very long journey.

units.leftText: Then the men of Israel sampled their provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the men took of their provision, and asked not counsel at the mouth of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
units.rightText: And Joshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them.

units.leftText: Three days after they had made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites learned that they were neighbors, living among them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they dwelt among them.

units.leftText: So the Israelites set out and on the third day arrived at their cities — Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel journeyed, and came unto their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

units.leftText: But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by Jehovah, the God of Israel. And all the congregation murmured against the princes.

units.leftText: All the leaders answered, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
units.rightText: But all the princes said unto all the congregation, We have sworn unto them by Jehovah, the God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.

units.leftText: This is how we will treat them: We will let them live, so that no wrath will fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.”
units.rightText: This we will do to them, and let them live; lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them.

units.leftText: They continued, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” So the leaders kept their promise.
units.rightText: And the princes said unto them, Let them live: so they became hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation, as the princes had spoken unto them.

units.leftText: Then Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said, “Why did you deceive us by telling us you live far away from us, when in fact you live among us?
units.rightText: And Joshua called for them, and he spake unto them, saying, Wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you; when ye dwell among us?

units.leftText: Now therefore you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”
units.rightText: Now therefore ye are cursed, and there shall never fail to be of you bondmen, both hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God.

units.leftText: The Gibeonites answered, “Your servants were told clearly that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants before you. So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.
units.rightText: And they answered Joshua, and said, Because it was certainly told thy servants, how that Jehovah thy God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you; therefore we were sore afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this thing.

units.leftText: Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”
units.rightText: And now, behold, we are in thy hand: as it seemeth good and right unto thee to do unto us, do.

units.leftText: So Joshua did this and delivered them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill the Gibeonites.
units.rightText: And so did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not.

units.leftText: On that day he made them woodcutters and water carriers, as they are to this day for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose.
units.rightText: And Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation, and for the altar of Jehovah, unto this day, in the place which he should choose.

units.leftText: Now Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction — doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king — and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living near them.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass, when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai, and had utterly destroyed it (as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king), and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among them;
leftNotes: 10:1 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 28, 35, 37, 39, and 40.

units.leftText: So Adoni-zedek and his people were greatly alarmed, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
