units.rightText: that they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty.

units.leftText: Therefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
units.rightText: Wherefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent unto Hoham king of Hebron, and unto Piram king of Jarmuth, and unto Japhia king of Lachish, and unto Debir king of Eglon, saying,

units.leftText: “Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon, because they have made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”
units.rightText: Come up unto me, and help me, and let us smite Gibeon; for it hath made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.

units.leftText: So the five kings of the Amorites— the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon— joined forces and advanced with all their armies. They camped before Gibeon and made war against it.
units.rightText: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their hosts, and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it.

units.leftText: Then the men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: “Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us! Help us, because all the kings of the Amorites from the hill country have joined forces against us.”
units.rightText: And the men of Gibeon sent unto Joshua to the camp to Gilgal, saying, Slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us: for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the hill-country are gathered together against us.

units.leftText: So Joshua and his whole army, including all the mighty men of valor, came from Gilgal.
units.rightText: So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand against you.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thy hands; there shall not a man of them stand before thee.

units.leftText: After marching all night from Gilgal, Joshua caught them by surprise.
units.rightText: Joshua therefore came upon them suddenly; for he went up from Gilgal all the night.

units.leftText: And the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who defeated them in a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursued them along the ascent to Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
units.rightText: And Jehovah discomfited them before Israel, and he slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah.

units.leftText: As they fled before Israel along the descent from Beth-horon to Azekah, the LORD cast down on them large hailstones from the sky, and more of them were killed by the hailstones than by the swords of the Israelites.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth-horon, that Jehovah cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died: they were more who died with the hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword.

units.leftText: On the day that the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD in the presence of Israel: “O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”
units.rightText: Then spake Joshua to Jehovah in the day when Jehovah delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; And thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon.

units.leftText: So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation took vengeance upon its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? “So the sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.”
units.rightText: And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, Until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jashar? And the sun stayed in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.
leftNotes: 10:13 Or triumphed over its enemies
10:13 Or the Book of the Upright One, commonly cited as Jasher

units.leftText: There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel.
units.rightText: And there was no day like that before it or after it, that Jehovah hearkened unto the voice of a man: for Jehovah fought for Israel.

units.leftText: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal. The Victory at Makkedah
units.rightText: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, unto the camp to Gilgal.

units.leftText: Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
units.rightText: And these five kings fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.

units.leftText: And Joshua was informed: “The five kings have been found; they are hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
units.rightText: And it was told Joshua, saying, The five kings are found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah.

units.leftText: So Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.
units.rightText: And Joshua said, Roll great stones unto the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to keep them:

units.leftText: But you, do not stop there. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand.”
units.rightText: but stay not ye; pursue after your enemies, and smite the hindmost of them; suffer them not to enter into their cities: for Jehovah your God hath delivered them into your hand.

units.leftText: So Joshua and the Israelites continued to inflict a terrible slaughter until they had finished them off, and the remaining survivors retreated to the fortified cities.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Joshua and the children of Israel had made an end of slaying them with a very great slaughter, till they were consumed, and the remnant which remained of them had entered into the fortified cities,

units.leftText: The whole army returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah, and no one dared to utter a word against the Israelites.
units.rightText: that all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace: none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”
units.rightText: Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring forth those five kings unto me out of the cave.

units.leftText: So they brought the five kings out of the cave — the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
units.rightText: And they did so, and brought forth those five kings unto him out of the cave, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.

units.leftText: When they had brought the kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had accompanied him, “Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” So the commanders came forward and put their feet on their necks.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they brought forth those kings unto Joshua, that Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said unto the chiefs of the men of war that went with him, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. And they came near, and put their feet upon the necks of them.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid or discouraged,” Joshua said. “Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto them, Fear not, nor be dismayed; be strong and of good courage: for thus shall Jehovah do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.

units.leftText: After this, Joshua struck down and killed the kings, and he hung their bodies on five trees and left them there until evening.
units.rightText: And afterward Joshua smote them, and put them to death, and hanged them on five trees: and they were hanging upon the trees until the evening.
leftNotes: 10:26 Or impaled their bodies on five poles; similarly in verse 27

units.leftText: At sunset Joshua ordered that they be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave in which they had hidden. Then large stones were placed against the mouth of the cave, and the stones are there to this day.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the time of the going down of the sun, that Joshua commanded, and they took them down off the trees, and cast them into the cave wherein they had hidden themselves, and laid great stones on the mouth of the cave, unto this very day.

units.leftText: On that day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it to the sword, along with its king. He devoted to destruction everyone in the city, leaving no survivors. So he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho. Conquest of the Southern Cities
units.rightText: And Joshua took Makkedah on that day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and the king thereof: he utterly destroyed them and all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining; and he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done unto the king of Jericho.

units.leftText: Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.
units.rightText: And Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, unto Libnah, and fought against Libnah:

units.leftText: And the LORD also delivered that city and its king into the hand of Israel, and Joshua put all the people to the sword, leaving no survivors. And he did to the king of Libnah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
units.rightText: and Jehovah delivered it also, and the king thereof, into the hand of Israel; and he smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining in it; and he did unto the king thereof as he had done unto the king of Jericho.

units.leftText: And Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish. They laid siege to it and fought against it.
units.rightText: And Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, unto Lachish, and encamped against it, and fought against it:

units.leftText: And the LORD delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He put all the people to the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
units.rightText: and Jehovah delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel; and he took it on the second day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls that were therein, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

units.leftText: At that time Horam king of Gezer went to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down along with his people, leaving no survivors.
units.rightText: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua smote him and his people, until he had left him none remaining.

units.leftText: So Joshua moved on from Lachish to Eglon, and all Israel with him. They laid siege to it and fought against it.
units.rightText: And Joshua passed from Lachish, and all Israel with him, unto Eglon; and they encamped against it, and fought against it;

units.leftText: That day they captured Eglon and put it to the sword, and Joshua devoted to destruction everyone in the city, just as he had done to Lachish.
units.rightText: and they took it on that day, and smote it with the edge of the sword; and all the souls that were therein he utterly destroyed that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

units.leftText: Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.
units.rightText: And Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, unto Hebron; and they fought against it:

units.leftText: They captured it and put to the sword its king, all its villages, and all the people. Joshua left no survivors, just as he had done at Eglon; he devoted to destruction Hebron and everyone in it.
units.rightText: and they took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and the king thereof, and all the cities thereof, and all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining, according to all that he had done to Eglon; but he utterly destroyed it, and all the souls that were therein.

units.leftText: Finally Joshua and all Israel with him turned toward Debir and fought against it.
units.rightText: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it:

units.leftText: And they captured Debir, its king, and all its villages. They put them to the sword and devoted to destruction everyone in the city, leaving no survivors. Joshua did to Debir and its king as he had done to Hebron and as he had done to Libnah and its king.
units.rightText: and he took it, and the king thereof, and all the cities thereof; and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein; he left none remaining: as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir, and to the king thereof; as he had done also to Libnah, and to the king thereof.

units.leftText: So Joshua conquered the whole region— the hill country, the Negev, the foothills, and the slopes, together with all their kings— leaving no survivors. He devoted to destruction everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
units.rightText: So Joshua smote all the land, the hill-country, and the South, and the lowland, and the slopes, and all their kings: he left none remaining, but he utterly destroyed all that breathed, as Jehovah, the God of Israel, commanded.
leftNotes: 10:40 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Joshua conquered the area from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
units.rightText: And Joshua smote them from Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even unto Gibeon.

units.leftText: And because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel, Joshua captured all these kings and their land in one campaign.
units.rightText: And all these kings and their land did Joshua take at one time, because Jehovah, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

units.leftText: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
units.rightText: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, unto the camp to Gilgal.

units.leftText: Now when Jabin king of Hazor heard about these things, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon; to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph;
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jabin king of Hazor heard thereof, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,

units.leftText: to the kings of the north in the mountains, in the Arabah south of Chinnereth, in the foothills, and in Naphoth-dor to the west;
units.rightText: and to the kings that were on the north, in the hill-country, and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, and in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
leftNotes: 11:2 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea; also in verse 16
11:2 Or in the heights of Dor; Naphoth-dor is a variant of Naphath-dor; see Joshua 12:23|JOS 12:23*.

units.leftText: to the Canaanites in the east and west; to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country; and to the Hivites at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
units.rightText: to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, and the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite in the hill-country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.

units.leftText: So these kings came out with all their armies, a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore, along with a great number of horses and chariots.
units.rightText: And they went out, they and all their hosts with them, much people, even as the sand that is upon the sea-shore in multitude, with horses and chariots very many.

units.leftText: All these kings joined forces and encamped at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
units.rightText: And all these kings met together; and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight with Israel.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for by this time tomorrow I will deliver all of them slain before Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and burn up their chariots.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Joshua, Be not afraid because of them; for to-morrow at this time will I deliver them up all slain before Israel: thou shalt hock their horses, and burn their chariots with fire.

units.leftText: So by the waters of Merom, Joshua and his whole army came upon them suddenly and attacked them,
units.rightText: So Joshua came, and all the people of war with him, against them by the waters of Merom suddenly, and fell upon them.

units.leftText: and the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, who struck them down and pursued them all the way to Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and eastward as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. They struck them down, leaving no survivors.
units.rightText: And Jehovah delivered them into the hand of Israel, and they smote them, and chased them unto great Sidon, and unto Misrephoth-maim, and unto the valley of Mizpeh eastward; and they smote them, until they left them none remaining.

units.leftText: Joshua treated them as the LORD had told him; he hamstrung their horses and burned up their chariots.
units.rightText: And Joshua did unto them as Jehovah bade him: he hocked their horses, and burnt their chariots with fire.

units.leftText: At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and put its king to the sword, because Hazor was formerly the head of all these kingdoms.
units.rightText: And Joshua turned back at that time, and took Hazor, and smote the king thereof with the sword: for Hazor beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms.

units.leftText: The Israelites put everyone in Hazor to the sword, devoting them to destruction. Nothing that breathed remained, and Joshua burned down Hazor itself.
units.rightText: And they smote all the souls that were therein with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them; there was none left that breathed: and he burnt Hazor with fire.
leftNotes: 11:11 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 12, 20, and 21.

units.leftText: Joshua captured all these kings and their cities and put them to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses the LORD’s servant had commanded.
units.rightText: And all the cities of those kings, and all the kings of them, did Joshua take, and he smote them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed them; as Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded.

units.leftText: Yet Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned.
units.rightText: But as for the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel burned none of them, save Hazor only; that did Joshua burn.

units.leftText: The Israelites took for themselves all the plunder and livestock of these cities, but they put all the people to the sword until they had completely destroyed them, not sparing anyone who breathed.
units.rightText: And all the spoil of these cities, and the cattle, the children of Israel took for a prey unto themselves; but every man they smote with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them, neither left they any that breathed.

units.leftText: As the LORD had commanded His servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua. That is what Joshua did, leaving nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses. Joshua Takes the Whole Land
units.rightText: As Jehovah commanded Moses his servant, so did Moses command Joshua: and so did Joshua; he left nothing undone of all that Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: So Joshua took this entire region: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the western foothills, the Arabah, and the mountains of Israel and their foothills,
units.rightText: So Joshua took all that land, the hill-country, and all the South, and all the land of Goshen, and the lowland, and the Arabah, and the hill-country of Israel, and the lowland of the same;

units.leftText: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon at the foot of Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down, putting them to death.
units.rightText: from mount Halak, that goeth up to Seir, even unto Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon under mount Hermon: and all their kings he took, and smote them, and put them to death.

units.leftText: Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long period of time.
units.rightText: Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.

units.leftText: No city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites living in Gibeon; all others were taken in battle.
units.rightText: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, save the Hivites the inhabitants of Gibeon: they took all in battle.

units.leftText: For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts to engage Israel in battle, so that they would be set apart for destruction and would receive no mercy, being annihilated as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: For it was of Jehovah to harden their hearts, to come against Israel in battle, that he might utterly destroy them, that they might have no favor, but that he might destroy them, as Jehovah commanded Moses.
leftNotes: 11:20 Or stiffen or strengthen

units.leftText: At that time Joshua proceeded to eliminate the Anakim from the hill country of Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction, along with their cities.
units.rightText: And Joshua came at that time, and cut off the Anakim from the hill-country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill-country of Judah, and from all the hill-country of Israel: Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities.

units.leftText: No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any survive.
units.rightText: There was none of the Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.

units.leftText: So Joshua took the entire land, in keeping with all that the LORD had spoken to Moses. And Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to the allotments to their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.
units.rightText: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that Jehovah spake unto Moses; and Joshua gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

units.leftText: Now these are the kings of the land whom the Israelites struck down and whose lands they took beyond the Jordan to the east, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, including all the Arabah eastward:
units.rightText: Now these are the kings of the land, whom the children of Israel smote, and possessed their land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrising, from the valley of the Arnon unto mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

units.leftText: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along the middle of the valley, up to the Jabbok River (the border of the Ammonites), that is, half of Gilead,
units.rightText: Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and half Gilead, even unto the river Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon;

units.leftText: as well as the Arabah east of the Sea of Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea ), eastward through Beth-jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
units.rightText: and the Arabah unto the sea of Chinneroth, eastward, and unto the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth-jeshimoth; and on the south, under the slopes of Pisgah:
leftNotes: 12:3 That is, the Sea of Galilee
12:3 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: And Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
units.rightText: and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
leftNotes: 12:4 LXX; Hebrew And the territory of Og king of Bashan

units.rightText: and ruled in mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, unto the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

units.leftText: Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites had struck them down and given their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. The Kings Defeated West of the Jordan
units.rightText: Moses the servant of Jehovah and the children of Israel smote them: and Moses the servant of Jehovah gave it for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

units.leftText: the hill country, the foothills, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev — the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites):

units.rightText: the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty and one.

units.leftText: Now Joshua was old and well along in years, and the LORD said to him, “You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed.
units.rightText: Now Joshua was old and well stricken in years; and Jehovah said unto him, Thou art old and well stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed.

units.leftText: This is the land that remains:
units.rightText: This is the land that yet remaineth: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites;

units.leftText: from the Shihor east of Egypt to the territory of Ekron on the north (considered to be Canaanite territory)— that of the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, as well as that of the Avvites;
units.rightText: from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even unto the border of Ekron northward, which is reckoned to the Canaanites; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim,

units.leftText: to the south, all the land of the Canaanites, from Mearah of the Sidonians to Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorites;
units.rightText: on the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongeth to the Sidonians, unto Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
leftNotes: 13:4 Or Arah

units.leftText: the land of the Gebalites; and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
units.rightText: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrising, from Baal-gad under mount Hermon unto the entrance of Hamath;
leftNotes: 13:5 Or the area of Byblos

units.leftText: All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim — all the Sidonians — I Myself will drive out before the Israelites. Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you.
units.rightText: all the inhabitants of the hill-country from Lebanon unto Misrephoth-maim, even all the Sidonians; them will I drive out from before the children of Israel: only allot thou it unto Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee.

units.leftText: Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.” The Inheritance East of the Jordan (Numbers 32:1–42|NUM 32:1-42*; Deuteronomy 3:12–22|DEU 3:12-22*)
units.rightText: Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

units.leftText: The other half of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had received the inheritance Moses had given them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had assigned to them:
units.rightText: With him the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond the Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of Jehovah gave them:

units.leftText: The area from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, the whole plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,
units.rightText: from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon;

units.leftText: and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
units.rightText: and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, unto the border of the children of Ammon;

units.leftText: also Gilead and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah—
units.rightText: and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all mount Hermon, and all Bashan unto Salecah;

units.leftText: the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who had reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei and had remained as a remnant of the Rephaim.
units.rightText: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (the same was left of the remnant of the Rephaim); for these did Moses smite, and drove them out.

units.leftText: but the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day.
units.rightText: Nevertheless the children of Israel drove not out the Geshurites, nor the Maacathites: but Geshur and Maacath dwell in the midst of Israel unto this day.

units.leftText: To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them. Reuben’s Inheritance
units.rightText: Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance; the offerings of Jehovah, the God of Israel, made by fire are his inheritance, as he spake unto him.

units.leftText: This is what Moses had given to the clans of the tribe of Reuben:
units.rightText: And Moses gave unto the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their families.

units.leftText: The territory from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, to the whole plateau beyond Medeba,
units.rightText: And their border was from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain by Medeba;

units.leftText: to Heshbon and all its cities on the plateau, including Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
units.rightText: Heshbon, and all its cities that are in the plain; Dibon, and Bamoth-baal, and Beth-baal-meon,

units.leftText: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
units.rightText: and Jahaz, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath,

units.leftText: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
units.rightText: and Kiriathaim, and Sibmah, and Zereth-shahar in the mount of the valley,

units.leftText: Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth—
units.rightText: and Beth-peor, and the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth,

units.leftText: all the cities of the plateau and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon until Moses killed him and the chiefs of Midian (Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba), the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
units.rightText: and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses smote with the chiefs of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, that dwelt in the land.

units.leftText: The Israelites also killed the diviner Balaam son of Beor along with the others they put to the sword.
units.rightText: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among the rest of their slain.

units.leftText: And the border of the Reubenites was the bank of the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the clans of the Reubenites, including the cities and villages. Gad’s Inheritance
units.rightText: And the border of the children of Reuben was the Jordan, and the border thereof. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their families, the cities and the villages thereof.

units.leftText: This is what Moses had given to the clans of the tribe of Gad:
units.rightText: And Moses gave unto the tribe of Gad, unto the children of Gad, according to their families.

units.leftText: The territory of Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah;
units.rightText: And their border was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah;

units.leftText: the territory from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;
units.rightText: and from Heshbon unto Ramath-mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir;

units.leftText: and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon (the territory on the east side of the Jordan up to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth ).
units.rightText: and in the valley, Beth-haram, and Beth-nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and the border thereof, unto the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastward.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the Gadites, including the cities and villages. Manasseh’s Eastern Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and the villages thereof.

units.leftText: This is what Moses had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, to half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh:
units.rightText: And Moses gave inheritance unto the half-tribe of Manasseh: and it was for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.

units.leftText: The territory from Mahanaim through all Bashan— all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, including all the towns of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
units.rightText: And their border was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair, which are in Bashan, threescore cities:

units.leftText: half of Gilead; and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan. All this was for the clans of the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, that is, half of the descendants of Machir.
units.rightText: and half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.

units.leftText: These were the portions Moses had given them on the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho.
units.rightText: These are the inheritances which Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward.

units.leftText: To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them.
units.rightText: But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: Jehovah, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spake unto them.

units.leftText: Now these are the portions that the Israelites inherited in the land of Canaan, as distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: And these are the inheritances which the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed unto them,

units.leftText: Their inheritance was assigned by lot for the nine and a half tribes, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
units.rightText: by the lot of their inheritance, as Jehovah commanded by Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half-tribe.

units.leftText: For Moses had given the inheritance east of the Jordan to the other two and a half tribes. But he granted no inheritance among them to the Levites.
units.rightText: For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan: but unto the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

units.leftText: The descendants of Joseph became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. And no portion of the land was given to the Levites, except for cities in which to live, along with pasturelands for their flocks and herds.
units.rightText: For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim: and they gave no portion unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in, with the suburbs thereof for their cattle and for their substance.

units.leftText: So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land. Caleb Requests Hebron
units.rightText: As Jehovah commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did; and they divided the land.

units.leftText: Then the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea about you and me.
units.rightText: Then the children of Judah drew nigh unto Joshua in Gilgal: and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said unto him, Thou knowest the thing that Jehovah spake unto Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning thee in Kadesh-barnea.

units.leftText: I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back to him an honest report.
units.rightText: Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of Jehovah sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land; and I brought him word again as it was in my heart.

units.leftText: Although my brothers who went with me made the hearts of the people melt with fear, I remained loyal to the LORD my God.
units.rightText: Nevertheless my brethren that went up with me made the heart of the people melt; but I wholly followed Jehovah my God.

units.leftText: On that day Moses swore to me, saying, ‘Surely the land on which you have set foot will be an inheritance to you and your children forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God.’
units.rightText: And Moses sware on that day, saying, Surely the land whereon thy foot hath trodden shall be an inheritance to thee and to thy children for ever, because thou hast wholly followed Jehovah my God.

units.leftText: Now behold, as the LORD promised, He has kept me alive these forty-five years since He spoke this word to Moses, while Israel wandered in the wilderness. So here I am today, eighty-five years old,
units.rightText: And now, behold, Jehovah hath kept me alive, as he spake, these forty and five years, from the time that Jehovah spake this word unto Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old.

units.leftText: still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. As my strength was then, so it is now for war, for going out, and for coming in.
units.rightText: As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, and to go out and to come in.

units.leftText: Now therefore give me this hill country that the LORD promised me on that day, for you yourself heard then that the Anakim were there, with great and fortified cities. Perhaps with the LORD’s help I will drive them out, as the LORD has spoken.”
units.rightText: Now therefore give me this hill-country, whereof Jehovah spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakim were there, and cities great and fortified: it may be that Jehovah will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as Jehovah spake.

units.leftText: Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
units.rightText: And Joshua blessed him; and he gave Hebron unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.

units.leftText: Therefore Hebron belongs to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he wholly followed the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite unto this day; because that he wholly followed Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: (Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim.) Then the land had rest from war.
units.rightText: Now the name of Hebron beforetime was Kiriath-arba; which Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

units.leftText: Now the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah extended to the border of Edom, to the Wilderness of Zin at the extreme southern boundary:
units.rightText: And the lot for the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families was unto the border of Edom, even to the wilderness of Zin southward, at the uttermost part of the south.

units.leftText: Their southern border started at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea,
units.rightText: And their south border was from the uttermost part of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looketh southward;
leftNotes: 15:2 That is, the Dead Sea; also in verse 5

units.leftText: proceeded south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continued on to Zin, went over to the south of Kadesh-barnea, ran past Hezron up to Addar, and curved toward Karka.
units.rightText: and it went out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and went up by the south of Kadesh-barnea, and passed along by Hezron, and went up to Addar, and turned about to Karka;
leftNotes: 15:3 Or the Ascent of Scorpions or Scorpion Pass

units.leftText: It proceeded to Azmon, joined the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the Sea. This was their southern border.
units.rightText: and it passed along to Azmon, and went out at the brook of Egypt; and the goings out of the border were at the sea: this shall be your south border.
leftNotes: 15:4 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea; also in verses 11, 12, and 47
15:4 LXX; Hebrew your

units.leftText: The eastern border was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan.
units.rightText: And the east border was the Salt Sea, even unto the end of the Jordan. And the border of the north quarter was from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan;

units.leftText: went up to Beth-hoglah, proceeded north of Beth-arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
units.rightText: and the border went up to Beth-hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth-arabah; and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben;

units.leftText: Then the border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turning north to Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adummim south of the ravine. It continued along the waters of En-shemesh and came out at En-rogel.
units.rightText: and the border went up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that is over against the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south side of the river; and the border passed along to the waters of En-shemesh, and the goings out thereof were at En-rogel;

units.leftText: From there the border went up the Valley of Ben-hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusites (that is, Jerusalem) and ascended to the top of the hill that faces the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: and the border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the side of the Jebusite southward (the same is Jerusalem); and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lieth before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the uttermost part of the vale of Rephaim northward;

units.leftText: From the hilltop the border curved to the spring of the Waters of Nephtoah, proceeded to the cities of Mount Ephron, and then bent around toward Baalah (that is, Kiriath-jearim).
units.rightText: and the border extended from the top of the mountain unto the fountain of the waters of Nephtoah, and went out to the cities of mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah (the same is Kiriath-jearim);

units.leftText: The border curled westward from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim (that is, Chesalon), went down to Beth-shemesh, and crossed to Timnah.
units.rightText: and the border turned about from Baalah westward unto mount Seir, and passed along unto the side of mount Jearim on the north (the same is Chesalon), and went down to Beth-shemesh, and passed along by Timnah;

units.leftText: Then it went out to the northern slope of Ekron, curved toward Shikkeron, proceeded to Mount Baalah, went on to Jabneel, and ended at the Sea.
units.rightText: and the border went out unto the side of Ekron northward; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passed along to mount Baalah, and went out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border were at the sea.

units.leftText: And the western border was the coastline of the Great Sea. These are the boundaries around the clans of the descendants of Judah. Caleb’s Portion and Conquest (Judges 1:8–26|JDG 1:8-26*)
units.rightText: And the west border was to the great sea, and the border thereof. This is the border of the children of Judah round about according to their families.

units.leftText: According to the LORD’s command to him, Joshua gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among the sons of Judah — Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron. (Arba was the forefather of Anak.)
units.rightText: And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of Jehovah to Joshua, even Kiriath-arba, which Arba was the father of Anak (the same is Hebron).

units.leftText: And Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak — the descendants of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
units.rightText: And Caleb drove out thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.

units.leftText: From there he marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).
units.rightText: And he went up thence against the inhabitants of Debir: now the name of Debir beforetime was Kiriath-sepher.

units.leftText: And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”
units.rightText: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.

units.leftText: So Othniel son of Caleb’s brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.
units.rightText: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.

units.leftText: One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from off her ass; and Caleb said, What wouldest thou?
leftNotes: 15:18 Hebrew and some LXX manuscripts; other LXX manuscripts and he urged her; see Judges 1:14|JDG 1:14*.

units.leftText: “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.” So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs. The Cities of Judah
units.rightText: And she said, Give me a blessing; for that thou hast set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

units.leftText: This is the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Judah.
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.

units.leftText: These were the southernmost cities of the tribe of Judah in the Negev toward the border of Edom:
units.rightText: And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the border of Edom in the South were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,

units.leftText: Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
units.rightText: and Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah,

units.leftText: Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
units.rightText: and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan,

units.leftText: Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
units.rightText: Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth,

units.leftText: Hazor-hadattah, Kerioth-hezron (that is, Hazor),
units.rightText: and Hazor-hadattah, and Kerioth-hezron (the same is Hazor),

units.leftText: Amam, Shema, Moladah,
units.rightText: Amam, and Shema, and Moladah,

units.leftText: Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet,
units.rightText: and Hazar-gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-pelet,

units.leftText: Hazar-shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
units.rightText: and Hazar-shual, and Beer-sheba, and Biziothiah,

units.leftText: Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
units.rightText: Baalah, and Iim, and Ezem,

units.leftText: Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
units.rightText: and Eltolad, and Chesil, and Hormah,

units.leftText: Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
units.rightText: and Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah,

units.leftText: Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon— twenty-nine cities in all, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and Ain, and Rimmon: all the cities are twenty and nine, with their villages.

units.leftText: These were in the foothills:
units.rightText: In the lowland, Eshtaol, and Zorah, and Ashnah,
leftNotes: 15:33 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
units.rightText: and Zanoah, and En-gannim, Tappuah, and Enam,

units.leftText: Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
units.rightText: Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah,

units.leftText: Shaaraim, Adithaim, and Gederah (or Gederothaim)— fourteen cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Shaaraim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad,
units.rightText: Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-gad,

units.leftText: Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel,
units.rightText: and Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel,

units.leftText: Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
units.rightText: Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon,

units.leftText: Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish,
units.rightText: and Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Chitlish,

units.leftText: Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah— sixteen cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Gederoth, Beth-dagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
units.rightText: Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan,

units.leftText: Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
units.rightText: and Iphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib,

units.leftText: Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah— nine cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Ekron, with its towns and villages;
units.rightText: Ekron, with its towns and its villages;

units.leftText: from Ekron to the sea, all the cities near Ashdod, along with their villages;
units.rightText: from Ekron even unto the sea, all that were by the side of Ashdod, with their villages.

units.leftText: Ashdod, with its towns and villages; Gaza, with its towns and villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt and the coastline of the Great Sea.
units.rightText: Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; unto the brook of Egypt, and the great sea, and the border thereof.

units.leftText: These were in the hill country:
units.rightText: And in the hill-country, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh,

units.leftText: Dannah, Kiriath-sannah (that is, Debir),
units.rightText: and Dannah, and Kiriath-sannah (the same is Debir),

units.leftText: Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
units.rightText: and Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim,

units.leftText: Goshen, Holon, and Giloh— eleven cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
units.rightText: Arab, and Dumah, and Eshan,

units.leftText: Janim, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah,
units.rightText: and Janim, and Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah,

units.leftText: Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior— nine cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Humtah, and Kiriath-arba (the same is Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
units.rightText: Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Jutah,

units.leftText: Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
units.rightText: and Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah,

units.leftText: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah— ten cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Halhul, Beth-zur, Gedor,
units.rightText: Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor,

units.leftText: Maarath, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon— six cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Maarath, and Beth-anoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages.

units.leftText: Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim), and Rabbah— two cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: Kiriath-baal (the same is Kiriath-jearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages.

units.leftText: These were in the wilderness:
units.rightText: In the wilderness, Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah,

units.leftText: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi— six cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Nibshan, and the City of Salt, and En-gedi; six cities with their villages.

units.leftText: But the descendants of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah.
units.rightText: And as for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.

units.leftText: The allotment for the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east, through the wilderness that goes up from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
units.rightText: And the lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill-country to Beth-el;

units.leftText: It went on from Bethel (that is, Luz) and proceeded to the border of the Archites in Ataroth.
units.rightText: and it went out from Beth-el to Luz, and passed along unto the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
leftNotes: 16:2 LXX (See also Joshua 18:13|JOS 18:13*); Hebrew from Bethel to Luz

units.leftText: Then it descended westward to the border of the Japhletites as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and on to Gezer, and it ended at the Sea.
units.rightText: and it went down westward to the border of the Japhletites, unto the border of Beth-horon the nether, even unto Gezer; and the goings out thereof were at the sea.
leftNotes: 16:3 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea; also in verses 6 and 8

units.leftText: So Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, received their inheritance.
units.rightText: And the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.

units.leftText: This was the territory of the descendants of Ephraim by their clans:
units.rightText: And the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families was thus: the border of their inheritance eastward was Ataroth-addar, unto Beth-horon the upper;

units.leftText: and out toward the Sea. From Michmethath on the north it turned eastward toward Taanath-shiloh and passed by it to Janoah on the east.
units.rightText: and the border went out westward at Michmethath on the north; and the border turned about eastward unto Taanath-shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Janoah;

units.leftText: From Janoah it went down to Ataroth and Naarah, and then reached Jericho and came out at the Jordan.
units.rightText: and it went down from Janoah to Ataroth, and to Naarah, and reached unto Jericho, and went out at the Jordan.

units.leftText: From Tappuah the border went westward to the Brook of Kanah and ended at the Sea.
units.rightText: From Tappuah the border went along westward to the brook of Kanah; and the goings out thereof were at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families;

units.leftText: along with all the cities and villages set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of Manasseh.
units.rightText: together with the cities which were set apart for the children of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.

units.leftText: But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. So the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites to this day, but they are forced laborers.
units.rightText: And they drove not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer: but the Canaanites dwell in the midst of Ephraim unto this day, and are become servants to do taskwork.

units.leftText: Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh as Joseph’s firstborn son, namely for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh and father of the Gileadites, who had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war.
units.rightText: And this was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the first-born of Joseph. As for Machir the first-born of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

units.leftText: So this allotment was for the rest of the descendants of Manasseh — the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These are the other male descendants of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph.
units.rightText: So the lot was for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their families.
leftNotes: 17:2 Abiezer is a variant of Iezer; see Numbers 26:30|NUM 26:30*.

units.leftText: But Zelophehad son of Hepher (the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh) had no sons but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
units.rightText: But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

units.leftText: They approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.”
units.rightText: And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, Jehovah commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren: therefore according to the commandment of Jehovah he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

units.leftText: Thus ten shares fell to Manasseh, in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan,
units.rightText: And there fell ten parts to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan;

units.leftText: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. And the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
units.rightText: because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons. And the land of Gilead belonged unto the rest of the sons of Manasseh.

units.leftText: Now the border of Manasseh went from Asher to Michmethath near Shechem, then southward to include the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
units.rightText: And the border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which is before Shechem; and the border went along to the right hand, unto the inhabitants of En-tappuah.

units.leftText: The region of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to Ephraim.
units.rightText: The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh; but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.

units.leftText: From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah. There were cities belonging to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh, but the border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook and ended at the Sea.
units.rightText: And the border went down unto the brook of Kanah, southward of the brook: these cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh: and the border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook, and the goings out thereof were at the sea:
leftNotes: 17:9 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea; also in verse 10

units.leftText: Ephraim’s territory was to the south, and Manasseh’s was to the north, having the Sea as its border and adjoining Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
units.rightText: southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea was his border; and they reached to Asher on the north, and to Issachar on the east.

units.leftText: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh was assigned Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor (that is, Naphath), Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, each with their surrounding settlements.
units.rightText: And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth-shean and its towns, and Ibleam and its towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, and the inhabitants of En-dor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns, even the three heights.

units.leftText: But the descendants of Manasseh were unable to occupy these cities, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in this land.
units.rightText: Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

units.leftText: However, when the Israelites grew stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor; but they failed to drive them out completely.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel were waxed strong, that they put the Canaanites to taskwork, and did not utterly drive them out.

units.leftText: Then the sons of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance? We have many people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly.”
units.rightText: And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one part for an inheritance, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as hitherto Jehovah hath blessed me?

units.leftText: Joshua answered them, “If you have so many people that the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto them, If thou be a great people, get thee up to the forest, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill-country of Ephraim is too narrow for thee.

units.leftText: “The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied, “and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
units.rightText: And the children of Joseph said, The hill-country is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are in Beth-shean and its towns, and they who are in the valley of Jezreel.

units.leftText: So Joshua said to the house of Joseph — to Ephraim and Manasseh — “You have many people and great strength. You shall not have just one allotment,
units.rightText: And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great power; thou shalt not have one lot only:

units.leftText: because the hill country will be yours as well. It is a forest; clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours. Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out.”
units.rightText: but the hill-country shall be thine; for though it is a forest, thou shalt cut it down, and the goings out thereof shall be thine; for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong.

units.leftText: Then the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there. And though the land was subdued before them,
units.rightText: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the tent of meeting there: and the land was subdued before them.

units.leftText: there were still seven tribes of Israel who had not yet received their inheritance.
units.rightText: And there remained among the children of Israel seven tribes, which had not yet divided their inheritance.

units.leftText: So Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the children of Israel, How long are ye slack to go in to possess the land, which Jehovah, the God of your fathers, hath given you?

units.leftText: Appoint three men from each tribe, and I will send them out to survey the land and map it out, according to the inheritance of each. Then they will return to me
units.rightText: Appoint for you three men of each tribe: and I will send them, and they shall arise, and walk through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance; and they shall come unto me.

units.leftText: and divide the land into seven portions. Judah shall remain in their territory in the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain in their territory in the north.
units.rightText: And they shall divide it into seven portions: Judah shall abide in his border on the south, and the house of Joseph shall abide in their border on the north.

units.leftText: When you have mapped out the seven portions of land and brought it to me, I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God.
units.rightText: And ye shall describe the land into seven portions, and bring the description hither to me; and I will cast lots for you here before Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: The Levites, however, have no portion among you, because their inheritance is the priesthood of the LORD. And Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received the inheritance that Moses the servant of the LORD gave them beyond the Jordan to the east.”
units.rightText: For the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of Jehovah is their inheritance: and Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan eastward, which Moses the servant of Jehovah gave them.

units.leftText: As the men got up to go out, Joshua commanded them to map out the land, saying, “Go and survey the land, map it out, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here in Shiloh in the presence of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And the men arose, and went: and Joshua charged them that went to describe the land, saying, Go and walk through the land, and describe it, and come again to me; and I will cast lots for you here before Jehovah in Shiloh.

units.leftText: So the men departed and went throughout the land, mapping it city by city into seven portions. Then they returned with the document to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
units.rightText: And the men went and passed through the land, and described it by cities into seven portions in a book; and they came to Joshua unto the camp at Shiloh.

units.leftText: And Joshua cast lots for them in the presence of the LORD at Shiloh, where he distributed the land to the Israelites according to their divisions. Benjamin’s Inheritance
units.rightText: And Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before Jehovah: and there Joshua divided the land unto the children of Israel according to their divisions.

units.leftText: The first lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Benjamin. Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Judah and Joseph:
units.rightText: And the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families: and the border of their lot went out between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.

units.leftText: On the north side their border began at the Jordan, went up past the northern slope of Jericho, headed west through the hill country, and came out at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
units.rightText: And their border on the north quarter was from the Jordan; and the border went up to the side of Jericho on the north, and went up through the hill-country westward; and the goings out thereof were at the wilderness of Beth-aven.

units.leftText: From there the border crossed over to the southern slope of Luz (that is, Bethel) and went down to Ataroth-addar on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.
units.rightText: And the border passed along from thence to Luz, to the side of Luz (the same is Beth-el), southward; and the border went down to Ataroth-addar, by the mountain that lieth on the south of Beth-horon the nether.

units.leftText: On the west side the border curved southward from the hill facing Beth-horon on the south and came out at Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim), a city of the sons of Judah. This was the western side.
units.rightText: And the border extended thence, and turned about on the west quarter southward, from the mountain that lieth before Beth-horon southward; and the goings out thereof were at Kiriath-baal (the same is Kiriath-jearim), a city of the children of Judah: this was the west quarter.

units.leftText: On the south side the border began at the outskirts of Kiriath-jearim and extended westward to the spring at the Waters of Nephtoah.
units.rightText: And the south quarter was from the uttermost part of Kiriath-jearim; and the border went out westward, and went out to the fountain of the waters of Nephtoah;

units.leftText: Then it went down to the foot of the hill that faces the Valley of Ben-hinnom at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim and ran down the Valley of Hinnom toward the southern slope of the Jebusites and downward to En-rogel.
units.rightText: and the border went down to the uttermost part of the mountain that lieth before the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the vale of Rephaim northward; and it went down to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite southward, and went down to En-rogel;

units.leftText: From there it curved northward and proceeded to En-shemesh and on to Geliloth facing the Ascent of Adummim, and continued down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
units.rightText: and it extended northward, and went out at En-shemesh, and went out to Geliloth, which is over against the ascent of Adummim; and it went down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben;

units.leftText: Then it went on to the northern slope of Beth-arabah and went down into the valley.
units.rightText: and it passed along to the side over against the Arabah northward, and went down unto the Arabah;
leftNotes: 18:18 LXX; Hebrew slope facing the Arabah

units.leftText: The border continued to the northern slope of Beth-hoglah and came out at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan. This was the southern border.
units.rightText: and the border passed along to the side of Beth-hoglah northward; and the goings out of the border were at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan: this was the south border.
leftNotes: 18:19 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: On the east side the border was the Jordan. These were the borders around the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benjamin.
units.rightText: And the Jordan was the border of it on the east quarter. This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin, by the borders thereof round about, according to their families.

units.leftText: These were the cities of the clans of the tribe of Benjamin:
units.rightText: Now the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their families were Jericho, and Beth-hoglah, and Emek-keziz,

units.leftText: Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
units.rightText: and Beth-arabah, and Zemaraim, and Beth-el,

units.leftText: Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
units.rightText: and Avvim, and Parah, and Ophrah,

units.leftText: Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba— twelve cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Chephar-ammoni, and Ophni, and Geba; twelve cities with their villages:

units.leftText: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
units.rightText: Gibeon, and Ramah, and Beeroth,

units.leftText: Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,
units.rightText: and Mizpeh, and Chephirah, and Mozah,

units.leftText: Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
units.rightText: and Rekem, and Irpeel, and Taralah,

units.leftText: Zelah, Haeleph, Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath-jearim — fourteen cities, along with their villages. This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benjamin.
units.rightText: and Zelah, Eleph, and the Jebusite (the same is Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kiriath; fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families.
leftNotes: 18:28 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew the Jebusite
18:28 Hebrew Gibeath
18:28 LXX; Hebrew Kiriath

units.leftText: The second lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Simeon:
units.rightText: And the second lot came out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance was in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Judah.

units.leftText: and included Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
units.rightText: And they had for their inheritance Beer-sheba, or Sheba, and Moladah,

units.leftText: Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,
units.rightText: and Hazar-shual, and Balah, and Ezem,

units.leftText: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
units.rightText: and Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah,

units.leftText: Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,
units.rightText: and Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah,

units.leftText: Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen— thirteen cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with their villages:

units.leftText: Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan— four cities, along with their villages,
units.rightText: Ain, Rimmon, and Ether, and Ashan; four cities with their villages:

units.leftText: and all the villages surrounding these cities as far as Baalath-beer (Ramah of the Negev).
units.rightText: and all the villages that were round about these cities to Baalath-beer, Ramah of the South. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families.

units.leftText: The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the territory of Judah, because the share for Judah’s descendants was too large for them. So the Simeonites received an inheritance within Judah’s portion. Zebulun’s Inheritance
units.rightText: Out of the part of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon; for the portion of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had inheritance in the midst of their inheritance.

units.leftText: The third lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Zebulun:
units.rightText: And the third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families. And the border of their inheritance was unto Sarid;

units.leftText: It went up westward to Maralah, reached Dabbesheth, and met the brook east of Jokneam.
units.rightText: and their border went up westward, even to Maralah, and reached to Dabbesheth; and it reached to the brook that is before Jokneam;

units.leftText: From Sarid it turned eastward along the border of Chisloth-tabor and went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.
units.rightText: and it turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrising unto the border of Chisloth-tabor; and it went out to Daberath, and went up to Japhia;

units.leftText: From there it crossed eastward to Gath-hepher and to Eth-kazin; it extended to Rimmon and curved around toward Neah.
units.rightText: and from thence it passed along eastward to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin; and it went out at Rimmon which stretcheth unto Neah;

units.leftText: Then the border circled around the north side of Neah to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
units.rightText: and the border turned about it on the north to Hannathon; and the goings out thereof were at the valley of Iphtah-el;

units.leftText: It also included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem. There were twelve cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Kattath, and Nahalal, and Shimron, and Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Zebulun, including these cities and their villages. Issachar’s Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities with their villages.

units.leftText: The fourth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Issachar:
units.rightText: The fourth lot came out for Issachar, even for the children of Issachar according to their families.

units.leftText: Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
units.rightText: And their border was unto Jezreel, and Chesulloth, and Shunem,

units.leftText: Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
units.rightText: and Hapharaim, and Shion, and Anaharath,

units.leftText: Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
units.rightText: and Rabbith, and Kishion, and Ebez,

units.leftText: Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.
units.rightText: and Remeth, and Engannim, and En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez,

units.leftText: The border reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and ended at the Jordan. There were sixteen cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and the border reached to Tabor, and Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh; and the goings out of their border were at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Issachar, including these cities and their villages. Asher’s Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities with their villages.

units.leftText: The fifth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Asher:
units.rightText: And the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families.

units.leftText: Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
units.rightText: And their border was Helkath, and Hali, and Beten, and Achshaph,
