units.leftText: Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath,
units.rightText: and Allammelech, and Amad, and Mishal; and it reached to Carmel westward, and to Shihor-libnath;

units.leftText: then turned eastward toward Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el, and went north to Beth-emek and Neiel, passing Cabul on the left.
units.rightText: and it turned toward the sunrising to Beth-dagon, and reached to Zebulun, and to the valley of Iphtah-el northward to Beth-emek and Neiel; and it went out to Cabul on the left hand,

units.leftText: It went on to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
units.rightText: and Ebron, and Rehob, and Hammon, and Kanah, even unto great Sidon;
leftNotes: 19:28 Some Hebrew manuscripts Abdon; see Joshua 21:30|JOS 21:30*.

units.leftText: The border then turned back toward Ramah as far as the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and came out at the Sea in the region of Achzib,
units.rightText: and the border turned to Ramah, and to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turned to Hosah; and the goings out thereof were at the sea by the region of Achzib;
leftNotes: 19:29 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob. There were twenty-two cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: Ummah also, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty and two cities with their villages.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Asher, including these cities and their villages. Naphtali’s Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities with their villages.

units.leftText: The sixth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Naphtali:
units.rightText: The sixth lot came out for the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families.

units.leftText: Their border started at Heleph and the great tree of Zaanannim, passing Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum and ending at the Jordan.
units.rightText: And their border was from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, unto Lakkum; and the goings out thereof were at the Jordan;

units.leftText: Then the border turned westward to Aznoth-tabor and ran from there to Hukkok, touching Zebulun on the south side, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
units.rightText: and the border turned westward to Aznoth-tabor, and went out from thence to Hukkok; and it reached to Zebulun on the south, and reached to Asher on the west, and to Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrising.
leftNotes: 19:34 Hebrew; LXX west, and the Jordan

units.leftText: The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
units.rightText: And the fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,

units.leftText: Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
units.rightText: and Adamah, and Ramah, and Hazor,

units.leftText: Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor,
units.rightText: and Kedesh, and Edrei, and En-hazor,

units.leftText: Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh. There were nineteen cities, along with their villages.
units.rightText: and Iron, and Migdal-el, Horem, and Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh; nineteen cities with their villages.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Naphtali, including these cities and their villages. Dan’s Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities with their villages.

units.leftText: The seventh lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Dan:
units.rightText: The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families.

units.leftText: The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
units.rightText: And the border of their inheritance was Zorah, and Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh,

units.leftText: Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
units.rightText: and Shaalabbin, and Aijalon, and Ithlah,

units.leftText: Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
units.rightText: and Elon, and Timnah, and Ekron,

units.leftText: Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
units.rightText: and Eltekeh, and Gibbethon, and Baalath,

units.leftText: Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon,
units.rightText: and Jehud, and Bene-berak, and Gath-rimmon,

units.leftText: Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, including the territory across from Joppa.
units.rightText: and Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border over against Joppa.

units.leftText: (Later, when the territory of the Danites was lost to them, they went up and fought against Leshem, captured it, and put it to the sword. So they took possession of Leshem, settled there, and renamed it after their father Dan.)
units.rightText: And the border of the children of Dan went out beyond them; for the children of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

units.leftText: This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Dan, including these cities and their villages. Joshua’s Inheritance
units.rightText: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities with their villages.

units.leftText: When they had finished distributing the land into its territories, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them,
units.rightText: So they made an end of distributing the land for inheritance by the borders thereof; and the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun in the midst of them:

units.leftText: as the LORD had commanded. They gave him the city of Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, as he requested. He rebuilt the city and settled in it.
units.rightText: according to the commandment of Jehovah they gave him the city which he asked, even Timnath-serah in the hill-country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and dwelt therein.
leftNotes: 19:50 Timnath-serah is also known as Timnath-heres; see Judges 2:9|JDG 2:9*.

units.leftText: These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families distributed by lot to the tribes of Israel at Shiloh before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing up the land.
units.rightText: These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting. So they made an end of dividing the land.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Joshua,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Joshua, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the Israelites to designate the cities of refuge, as I instructed you through Moses,
units.rightText: Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Assign you the cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by Moses,

units.leftText: so that anyone who kills another unintentionally or accidentally may flee there. These will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
units.rightText: that the manslayer that killeth any person unwittingly and unawares may flee thither: and they shall be unto you for a refuge from the avenger of blood.

units.leftText: When someone flees to one of these cities, stands at the entrance of the city gate, and states his case before its elders, they are to bring him into the city and give him a place to live among them.
units.rightText: And he shall flee unto one of those cities, and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city; and they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them.

units.leftText: Now if the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand, because that man killed his neighbor accidentally without prior malice.
units.rightText: And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver up the manslayer into his hand; because he smote his neighbor unawares, and hated him not beforetime.

units.leftText: He is to stay in that city until he stands trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest serving at that time. Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.”
units.rightText: And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the manslayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.

units.leftText: So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the hill country of Judah.
units.rightText: And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill-country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (the same is Hebron) in the hill-country of Judah.

units.leftText: And beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer on the wilderness plateau from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.
units.rightText: And beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

units.leftText: These are the cities appointed for all the Israelites and foreigners among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood prior to standing trial before the assembly.
units.rightText: These were the appointed cities for all the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person unwittingly might flee thither, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation.

units.leftText: Now the family heads of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the other tribes of Israel
units.rightText: Then came near the heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites unto Eleazar the priest, and unto Joshua the son of Nun, and unto the heads of fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel;

units.leftText: at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said to them, “The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock.”
units.rightText: and they spake unto them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, Jehovah commanded by Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with the suburbs thereof for our cattle.

units.leftText: So by the command of the LORD, the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance:
units.rightText: And the children of Israel gave unto the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of Jehovah, these cities with their suburbs.

units.leftText: The first lot came out for the Kohathite clans. The Levites who were descendants of Aaron the priest received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
units.rightText: And the lot came out for the families of the Kohathites: and the children of Aaron the priest, who were of the Levites, had by lot out of the tribe of Judah, and out of the tribe of the Simeonites, and out of the tribe of Benjamin, thirteen cities.

units.leftText: The remaining descendants of Kohath received ten cities by lot from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
units.rightText: And the rest of the children of Kohath had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim, and out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, ten cities.

units.leftText: The descendants of Gershon received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
units.rightText: And the children of Gershon had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.

units.leftText: And the descendants of Merari received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
units.rightText: The children of Merari according to their families had out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.

units.leftText: So the Israelites allotted to the Levites these cities, together with their pasturelands, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel gave by lot unto the Levites these cities with their suburbs, as Jehovah commanded by Moses.

units.leftText: From the tribes of Judah and Simeon, they designated these cities by name
units.rightText: And they gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities which are here mentioned by name:

units.leftText: to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot fell to them:
units.rightText: and they were for the children of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, who were of the children of Levi; for theirs was the first lot.

units.leftText: They gave them Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), with its surrounding pasturelands, in the hill country of Judah. (Arba was the father of Anak.)
units.rightText: And they gave them Kiriath-arba, which Arba was the father of Anak (the same is Hebron), in the hill-country of Judah, with the suburbs thereof round about it.

units.leftText: But they had given the fields and villages around the city to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
units.rightText: But the fields of the city, and the villages thereof, gave they to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession.

units.leftText: So to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave these cities, together with their pasturelands: Hebron, a city of refuge for the manslayer, Libnah,
units.rightText: And unto the children of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Libnah with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Jattir, Eshtemoa,
units.rightText: and Jattir with its suburbs, and Eshtemoa with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Holon, Debir,
units.rightText: and Holon with its suburbs, and Debir with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Ain, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh— nine cities from these two tribes, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: and Ain with its suburbs, and Juttah with its suburbs, and Beth-shemesh with its suburbs; nine cities out of those two tribes.

units.leftText: And from the tribe of Benjamin they gave them Gibeon, Geba,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its suburbs, Geba with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Anathoth, and Almon— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Anathoth with its suburbs, and Almon with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
units.rightText: All the cities of the children of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their suburbs.

units.leftText: The remaining Kohathite clans of the Levites were allotted these cities:
units.rightText: And the families of the children of Kohath, the Levites, even the rest of the children of Kohath, they had the cities of their lot out of the tribe of Ephraim.

units.leftText: they were given Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim (a city of refuge for the manslayer), Gezer,
units.rightText: And they gave them Shechem with its suburbs in the hill-country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Gezer with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Kibzaim, and Beth-horon— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: and Kibzaim with its suburbs, and Beth-horon with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: From the tribe of Dan they were given Elteke, Gibbethon,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Dan, Elteke with its suburbs, Gibbethon with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Aijalon, and Gath-rimmon— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Aijalon with its suburbs, Gath-rimmon with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh they were given Taanach and Gath-rimmon— two cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: And out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its suburbs, and Gath-rimmon with its suburbs; two cities.

units.leftText: In all, ten cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the rest of the Kohathite clans.
units.rightText: All the cities of the families of the rest of the children of Kohath were ten with their suburbs.

units.leftText: This is what the Levite clans of the Gershonites were given: From the half-tribe of Manasseh they were given Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge for the manslayer, and Beeshterah— two cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: And unto the children of Gershon, of the families of the Levites, out of the half-tribe of Manasseh they gave Golan in Bashan with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Be-eshterah with its suburbs; two cities.

units.leftText: From the tribe of Issachar they were given Kishion, Daberath,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its suburbs, Daberath with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Jarmuth, and En-gannim— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Jarmuth with its suburbs, En-gannim with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: From the tribe of Asher they were given Mishal, Abdon,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its suburbs, Abdon with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Helkath, and Rehob— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Helkath with its suburbs, and Rehob with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: And from the tribe of Naphtali they were given Kedesh in Galilee (a city of refuge for the manslayer), Hammoth-dor, and Kartan— three cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Hammoth-dor with its suburbs, and Kartan with its suburbs; three cities.

units.leftText: In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the Gershonite clans.
units.rightText: All the cities of the Gershonites according to their families were thirteen cities with their suburbs.

units.leftText: This is what the Merarite clan (the rest of the Levites) were given:
units.rightText: And unto the families of the children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its suburbs, and Kartah with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Dimnah, and Nahalal— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Dimnah with its suburbs, Nahalal with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: From the tribe of Reuben they were given Bezer, Jahaz,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with its suburbs, and Jahaz with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Kedemoth, and Mephaath— four cities, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Kedemoth with its suburbs, and Mephaath with its suburbs; four cities.

units.leftText: And from the tribe of Gad they were given Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for the manslayer, Mahanaim,
units.rightText: And out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Mahanaim with its suburbs,

units.leftText: Heshbon, and Jazer— four cities in all, together with their pasturelands.
units.rightText: Heshbon with its suburbs, Jazer with its suburbs; four cities in all.

units.leftText: In all, twelve cities were allotted to the clans of Merari, the remaining Levite clans.
units.rightText: All these were the cities of the children of Merari according to their families, even the rest of the families of the Levites; and their lot was twelve cities.

units.leftText: For the Levites, then, there were forty-eight cities in all, together with their pasturelands, within the territory of the Israelites.
units.rightText: All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs.

units.leftText: Each of these cities had its own surrounding pasturelands; this was true for all the cities.
units.rightText: These cities were every one with their suburbs round about them: thus it was with all these cities.

units.leftText: Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land He had sworn to give their fathers, and they took possession of it and settled in it.
units.rightText: So Jehovah gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein.

units.leftText: And the LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers. None of their enemies could stand against them, for the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand.
units.rightText: And Jehovah gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; Jehovah delivered all their enemies into their hand.

units.leftText: Not one of all the LORD’s good promises to the house of Israel had failed; everything was fulfilled.
units.rightText: There failed not aught of any good thing which Jehovah had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.

units.leftText: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh
units.rightText: Then Joshua called the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,

units.leftText: and told them, “You have done all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
units.rightText: and said unto them, Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded you, and have hearkened unto my voice in all that I commanded you:

units.leftText: All this time you have not deserted your brothers, up to this very day, but have kept the charge given you by the LORD your God.
units.rightText: ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: And now that the LORD your God has given your brothers rest as He promised them, you may return to your homes in the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you across the Jordan.
units.rightText: And now Jehovah your God hath given rest unto your brethren, as he spake unto them: therefore now turn ye, and get you unto your tents, unto the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of Jehovah gave you beyond the Jordan.

units.leftText: But be very careful to observe the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul.”
units.rightText: Only take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law which Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded you, to love Jehovah your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.

units.leftText: So Joshua blessed them and sent them on their way, and they went to their homes.
units.rightText: So Joshua blessed them, and sent them away; and they went unto their tents.

units.leftText: (To the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land on the west side of the Jordan among their brothers.) When Joshua sent them to their homes he blessed them,
units.rightText: Now to the one half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given inheritance in Bashan; but unto the other half gave Joshua among their brethren beyond the Jordan westward. Moreover when Joshua sent them away unto their tents, he blessed them,

units.leftText: saying, “Return to your homes with your great wealth, with immense herds of livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, iron, and very many clothes. Divide with your brothers the spoil of your enemies.” The Altar of Witness
units.rightText: and spake unto them, saying, Return with much wealth unto your tents, and with very much cattle, with silver, and with gold, and with brass, and with iron, and with very much raiment: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren.

units.leftText: So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan to return to their own land of Gilead, which they had acquired according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
units.rightText: And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned, and departed from the children of Israel out of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go unto the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, whereof they were possessed, according to the commandment of Jehovah by Moses.

units.leftText: And when they came to Geliloth near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an imposing altar there by the Jordan.
units.rightText: And when they came unto the region about the Jordan, that is in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look upon.
leftNotes: 22:10 Or to the circle of stones or to the region; similarly in verse 11

units.leftText: Then the Israelites received the report: “Behold, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar on the border of the land of Canaan, at Geliloth near the Jordan on the Israelite side.”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel heard say, Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar in the forefront of the land of Canaan, in the region about the Jordan, on the side that pertaineth to the children of Israel.

units.leftText: And when they heard this, the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh to go to war against them.
units.rightText: And when the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel gathered themselves together at Shiloh, to go up against them to war.

units.leftText: The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the land of Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest,

units.leftText: With him they sent ten chiefs — one family leader from each tribe of Israel, each the head of a family among the clans of Israel.
units.rightText: and with him ten princes, one prince of a fathers’ house for each of the tribes of Israel; and they were every one of them head of their fathers’ houses among the thousands of Israel.

units.leftText: They went to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them,
units.rightText: And they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, unto the land of Gilead, and they spake with them, saying,

units.leftText: “This is what the whole congregation of the LORD says: ‘What is this breach of faith you have committed today against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD and building for yourselves an altar, that you might rebel against the LORD this day?
units.rightText: Thus saith the whole congregation of Jehovah, What trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away this day from following Jehovah, in that ye have builded you an altar, to rebel this day against Jehovah?

units.leftText: Was not the sin of Peor enough for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day? It even brought a plague upon the congregation of the LORD.
units.rightText: Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves unto this day, although there came a plague upon the congregation of Jehovah,

units.leftText: And now, would you turn away from the LORD? If you rebel today against the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
units.rightText: that ye must turn away this day from following Jehovah? and it will be, seeing ye rebel to-day against Jehovah, that to-morrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel.

units.leftText: If indeed the land of your inheritance is unclean, then cross over to the land of the LORD’s possession, where the LORD’s tabernacle stands, and take possession of it among us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us by building for yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.
units.rightText: Howbeit, if the land of your possession be unclean, then pass ye over unto the land of the possession of Jehovah, wherein Jehovah’s tabernacle dwelleth, and take possession among us: but rebel not against Jehovah, nor rebel against us, in building you an altar besides the altar of Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: Was not Achan son of Zerah unfaithful regarding what was set apart for destruction, bringing wrath upon the whole congregation of Israel? Yet it was not only Achan who perished because of his sin!’”
units.rightText: Did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and wrath fell upon all the congregation of Israel? and that man perished not alone in his iniquity.
leftNotes: 22:20 Achan means troubler; also called Acharin 1 Chronicles 2:7|1CH 2:7*.
22:20 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the clans of Israel:
units.rightText: Then the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered, and spake unto the heads of the thousands of Israel,

units.leftText: “The LORD, the Mighty One, is God! The LORD, the Mighty One, is God! He knows, and may Israel also know. If this was in rebellion or breach of faith against the LORD, do not spare us today.
units.rightText: The Mighty One, God, Jehovah, the Mighty One, God, Jehovah, he knoweth; and Israel he shall know: if it be in rebellion, or if in trespass against Jehovah (save thou us not this day),

units.leftText: If we have built for ourselves an altar to turn away from Him and to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to sacrifice peace offerings on it, may the LORD Himself hold us accountable.
units.rightText: that we have built us an altar to turn away from following Jehovah; or if to offer thereon burnt-offering or meal-offering, or if to offer sacrifices of peace-offerings thereon, let Jehovah himself require it;

units.leftText: But in fact we have done this for fear that in the future your descendants might say to ours, ‘What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
units.rightText: and if we have not rather out of carefulness done this, and of purpose, saying, In time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with Jehovah, the God of Israel?

units.leftText: For the LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD!’ So your descendants could cause ours to stop fearing the LORD.
units.rightText: for Jehovah hath made the Jordan a border between us and you, ye children of Reuben and children of Gad; ye have no portion in Jehovah: so might your children make our children cease from fearing Jehovah.

units.leftText: That is why we said, ‘Let us take action and build an altar for ourselves, but not for burnt offerings or sacrifices.
units.rightText: Therefore we said, Let us now prepare to build us an altar, not for burnt-offering, nor for sacrifice:

units.leftText: Rather, let it be a witness between us and you and the generations to come, that we will worship the LORD in His presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings.’ Then in the future, your descendants cannot say to ours, ‘You have no share in the LORD!’
units.rightText: but it shall be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may do the service of Jehovah before him with our burnt-offerings, and with our sacrifices, and with our peace-offerings; that your children may not say to our children in time to come, Ye have no portion in Jehovah.

units.leftText: Therefore we said, ‘If they ever say this to us or to our descendants, we will answer: Look at the replica of the altar of the LORD that our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.’
units.rightText: Therefore said we, It shall be, when they so say to us or to our generations in time to come, that we shall say, Behold the pattern of the altar of Jehovah, which our fathers made, not for burnt-offering, nor for sacrifice; but it is a witness between us and you.

units.leftText: Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from Him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God, which stands before His tabernacle.”
units.rightText: Far be it from us that we should rebel against Jehovah, and turn away this day from following Jehovah, to build an altar for burnt-offering, for meal-offering, or for sacrifice, besides the altar of Jehovah our God that is before his tabernacle.

units.leftText: When Phinehas the priest and the chiefs of the congregation — the heads of Israel’s clans who were with him — heard what the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh had to say, they were satisfied.
units.rightText: And when Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the congregation, even the heads of the thousands of Israel that were with him, heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake, it pleased them well.

units.leftText: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, “Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against Him. Consequently, you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, This day we know that Jehovah is in the midst of us, because ye have not committed this trespass against Jehovah: now have ye delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, together with the other leaders, returned to the Israelites in the land of Canaan and brought back a report regarding the Reubenites and Gadites in the land of Gilead.
units.rightText: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, unto the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brought them word again.

units.leftText: The Israelites were satisfied with the report, and they blessed God and spoke no more about going to war against them to destroy the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
units.rightText: And the thing pleased the children of Israel; and the children of Israel blessed God, and spake no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land wherein the children of Reuben and the children of Gad dwelt.

units.leftText: So the Reubenites and Gadites named the altar Witness, for they said, “It is a witness between us that the LORD is God.”
units.rightText: And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed: For, said they, it is a witness between us that Jehovah is God.
leftNotes: 22:34 Literally named the altar, for

units.leftText: A long time after the LORD had given Israel rest from all the enemies around them, when Joshua was old and well along in years,
units.rightText: And it came to pass after many days, when Jehovah had given rest unto Israel from all their enemies round about, and Joshua was old and well stricken in years;

units.leftText: he summoned all Israel, including its elders, leaders, judges, and officers. “I am old and well along in years,” he said,
units.rightText: that Joshua called for all Israel, for their elders and for their heads, and for their judges and for their officers, and said unto them, I am old and well stricken in years:

units.leftText: “and you have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, because it was the LORD your God who fought for you.
units.rightText: and ye have seen all that Jehovah your God hath done unto all these nations because of you; for Jehovah your God, he it is that hath fought for you.

units.leftText: See, I have allotted as an inheritance to your tribes these remaining nations, including all the nations I have already cut off, from the Jordan westward to the Great Sea.
units.rightText: Behold, I have allotted unto you these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun.
leftNotes: 23:4 That is, the Mediterranean Sea

units.leftText: The LORD your God will push them out of your way and drive them out before you, so that you can take possession of their land, as the LORD your God promised you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah your God, he will thrust them out from before you, and drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess their land, as Jehovah your God spake unto you.

units.leftText: Be very strong, then, so that you can keep and obey all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right or to the left.
units.rightText: Therefore be ye very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left;

units.leftText: So you are not to associate with these nations that remain among you. You must not call on the names of their gods or swear by them, and you must not serve them or bow down to them.
units.rightText: that ye come not among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow down yourselves unto them;

units.leftText: Instead, you shall hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
units.rightText: but cleave unto Jehovah your God, as ye have done unto this day.

units.leftText: The LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before you, and to this day no one can stand against you.
units.rightText: For Jehovah hath driven out from before you great nations and strong: but as for you, no man hath stood before you unto this day.

units.leftText: One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.
units.rightText: One man of you shall chase a thousand; for Jehovah your God, he it is that fighteth for you, as he spake unto you.

units.leftText: Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Take good heed therefore unto yourselves, that ye love Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: For if you turn away and cling to the rest of these nations that remain among you, and if you intermarry and associate with them,
units.rightText: Else if ye do at all go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and make marriages with them, and go in unto them, and they to you;

units.leftText: know for sure that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you. Instead, they will become for you a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.
units.rightText: know for a certainty that Jehovah your God will no more drive these nations from out of your sight; but they shall be a snare and a trap unto you, and a scourge in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which Jehovah your God hath given you.

units.leftText: Now behold, today I am going the way of all the earth, and you know with all your heart and soul that not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.
units.rightText: And, behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts and in all your souls, that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which Jehovah your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass unto you, not one thing hath failed thereof.

units.leftText: But just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened, until He has destroyed you from this good land He has given you.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that as all the good things are come upon you of which Jehovah your God spake unto you, so will Jehovah bring upon you all the evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land which Jehovah your God hath given you.

units.leftText: If you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from this good land He has given you.”
units.rightText: When ye transgress the covenant of Jehovah your God, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods, and bow down yourselves to them; then will the anger of Jehovah be kindled against you, and ye shall perish quickly from off the good land which he hath given unto you.

units.leftText: Then Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders, leaders, judges, and officers of Israel, and they presented themselves before God.
units.rightText: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers; and they presented themselves before God.

units.leftText: And Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your fathers, including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived beyond the Euphrates and worshiped other gods.
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt of old time beyond the River, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nahor: and they served other gods.
leftNotes: 24:2 Hebrew the River; also in verses 3, 14, and 15

units.leftText: But I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his descendants. I gave him Isaac,
units.rightText: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.

units.leftText: and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau Mount Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
units.rightText: And I gave unto Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I gave unto Esau mount Seir, to possess it; and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt.

units.leftText: Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I afflicted the Egyptians by what I did there, and afterward I brought you out.
units.rightText: And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt, according to that which I did in the midst thereof: and afterward I brought you out.

units.leftText: When I brought your fathers out of Egypt and you reached the Red Sea, the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.
units.rightText: And I brought your fathers out of Egypt: and ye came unto the sea; and the Egyptians pursued after your fathers with chariots and with horsemen unto the Red Sea.
leftNotes: 24:6 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: So your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He put darkness between you and the Egyptians, over whom He brought the sea and engulfed them. Your very eyes saw what I did to the Egyptians. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
units.rightText: And when they cried out unto Jehovah, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them, and covered them; and your eyes saw what I did in Egypt: and ye dwelt in the wilderness many days.

units.leftText: Later, I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, but I delivered them into your hand, that you should possess their land when I destroyed them before you.
units.rightText: And I brought you into the land of the Amorites, that dwelt beyond the Jordan: and they fought with you; and I gave them into your hand, and ye possessed their land; and I destroyed them from before you.

units.leftText: Then Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, set out to fight against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you,
units.rightText: Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel: and he sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you;

units.leftText: but I would not listen to Balaam. So he blessed you again and again, and I delivered you from his hand.
units.rightText: but I would not hearken unto Balaam; therefore he blessed you still: so I delivered you out of his hand.

units.leftText: After this, you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I delivered them into your hand.
units.rightText: And ye went over the Jordan, and came unto Jericho: and the men of Jericho fought against you, the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I delivered them into your hand.

units.leftText: I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove out the two Amorite kings before you, but not by your own sword or bow.
units.rightText: And I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; not with thy sword, nor with thy bow.

units.leftText: So I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities that you did not build, and now you live in them and eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.’ Choose Whom You Will Serve (Deuteronomy 10:12–22|DEU 10:12-22*)
units.rightText: And I gave you a land whereon thou hadst not labored, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell therein; of vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth; cast aside the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
units.rightText: Now therefore fear Jehovah, and serve him in sincerity and in truth; and put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River, and in Egypt; and serve ye Jehovah.

units.leftText: But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!”
units.rightText: And if it seem evil unto you to serve Jehovah, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve Jehovah.

units.leftText: The people replied, “Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!
units.rightText: And the people answered and said, Far be it from us that we should forsake Jehovah, to serve other gods;

units.leftText: For the LORD our God brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed these great signs before our eyes. He also protected us throughout our journey and among all the nations through which we traveled.
units.rightText: for Jehovah our God, he it is that brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and that did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way wherein we went, and among all the peoples through the midst of whom we passed;

units.leftText: And the LORD drove out before us all the nations, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God!”
units.rightText: and Jehovah drove out from before us all the peoples, even the Amorites that dwelt in the land: therefore we also will serve Jehovah; for he is our God.

units.leftText: But Joshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve the LORD, for He is a holy God; He is a jealous God; He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins.
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye cannot serve Jehovah; for he is a holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgression nor your sins.

units.leftText: If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and bring disaster on you and consume you, even after He has been good to you.”
units.rightText: If ye forsake Jehovah, and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you evil, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.

units.leftText: “No!” replied the people. “We will serve the LORD!”
units.rightText: And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Joshua told them, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the LORD.” “We are witnesses!” they said.
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you Jehovah, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.

units.leftText: “Now, therefore,” he said, “get rid of the foreign gods among you and incline your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
units.rightText: Now therefore put away, said he, the foreign gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: So the people said to Joshua, “We will serve the LORD our God and obey His voice.”
units.rightText: And the people said unto Joshua, Jehovah our God will we serve, and unto his voice will we hearken.

units.leftText: On that day Joshua made a covenant for the people, and there at Shechem he established for them a statute and ordinance.
units.rightText: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.

units.leftText: Joshua recorded these things in the Book of the Law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak that was near the sanctuary of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he took a great stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 24:26 Or terebinth

units.leftText: And Joshua said to all the people, “You see this stone. It will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words the LORD has spoken to us, and it will be a witness against you if you ever deny your God.”
units.rightText: And Joshua said unto all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us; for it hath heard all the words of Jehovah which he spake unto us: it shall be therefore a witness against you, lest ye deny your God.

units.leftText: Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance. Joshua’s Death and Burial (Judges 2:6–9|JDG 2:6-9*)
units.rightText: So Joshua sent the people away, every man unto his inheritance.

units.leftText: Some time later, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Jehovah, died, being a hundred and ten years old.

units.leftText: And they buried him in the land of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
units.rightText: And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, which is in the hill-country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
leftNotes: 24:30 Timnath-serah is also known as Timnath-heres; see Judges 2:9|JDG 2:9*.

units.leftText: Israel had served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him and who had experienced all the works that the LORD had done for Israel.
units.rightText: And Israel served Jehovah all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, and had known all the work of Jehovah, that he had wrought for Israel.

units.leftText: And the bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up out of Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the plot of land that Jacob had purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver. So it became an inheritance for Joseph’s descendants.
units.rightText: And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money: and they became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.
leftNotes: 24:32 Hebrew a hundred kesitahs; the value or weight of the kesitah is no longer known.

units.leftText: Eleazar son of Aaron also died, and they buried him at Gibeah, which had been given to his son Phinehas in the hill country of Ephraim.
units.rightText: And Eleazar the son of Aaron died; and they buried him in the hill of Phinehas his son, which was given him in the hill-country of Ephraim.
